title: Meet The 20 Startups Selected For Google Play Accelerator India
title_bn: Meet The 20 Startups Selected For Google Play Accelerator India
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Alphabet-owned Google has picked 20 homegrown startups for the 2026 cohort of its “Google Play Accelerator India” programme. This is…
paragraph1: Alphabet-owned Google has picked 20 homegrown startups for the 2026 cohort of its “Google Play Accelerator India” programme. This is the third cohort of the programme, which was introduced in 2024. The startups are picked from sectors like edtech, healthtech, gaming, agritech, fintech, ecommerce, media and entertainment. The accelerator will offer a three-month, equity-free programme, and provide the selected startups with hands-on support across AI integration, app quality, security, growth, and monetisation. “Through Google Play Accelerator India, we want to support founders across the full journey, from product quality and AI integration to growth, security, monetisation, and global scale. The 2026 cohort reflects the ambition of Indian startups to build trusted, useful products for India and the world,” Google Play Partnerships managing director Aditya Swamy said. Here’s the new set of 20 Indian AI startups picked for the 2026 cohort of Google Play Accelerator India Chaupal Founded In: 2021 Founders: Balwinder Singh and Sandeep Bansal Headquarters: Chandigarh The regional OTT streaming platform offers movies, web series, short films, and original content primarily in Punjabi, Bhojpuri, and Haryanvi. The regional OTT streaming service is available as an add-on channel via Amazon Prime Video Channels.
paragraph2: ChennaiGames Founded In: 2018 Founders: Radhakrishnan Doss Mohan, Radhakrishnan Narendrababu, and Devaraj Revathi Headquarters: Chennai ChennaiGames is a mobile game development studio that builds and publishes casual, multiplayer games for Android and iOS. The studio’s portfolio includes titles such as MR RACER, MR RACER: Stunt Mania, 21 Rush, LudoX, and Banger – Football Free Kicks. Dalvoy Founded In: 2025 Founders: Ritik Agrawal, Akash Sharma Headquarters: Delhi NCR Dalvoy is an AI-powered edtech startup that develops personalised learning tools for competitive exam aspirants. Its platform acts as an AI mentor that creates customised study plans, generates practice questions and mock tests, evaluates mains answers with detailed feedback, identifies knowledge gaps, and provides personalised revision based on each student’s progress. Frontier Markets Founded In: 2011 Founders: Ajaita Shah Headquarters: Jaipur Frontier Markets is a rural social commerce and last-mile distribution platform that connects FMCG, healthcare, financial services, clean energy, and agriculture brands with rural consumers via a network of digitally-enabled women entrepreneurs in these areas. GAPE Labs Founded In: 2023 Founders: Naren Budhwani Headquarters: Bengaluru The AI-first mobile gaming studio combines AI with game development to deliver original, character-driven multiplayer games for global audiences. Arcado Champs, its flagship game, is a real-time multiplayer strategy game. Grape Founded In: 2022 Founders: Sharath Shambu, Neerja Mittersain Ravishankar Headquarters: Mumbai Grape fashion app is an AI-native fashion discovery platform that combines Pinterest-style inspiration, personal styling, and ecommerce within one app, rather than functioning as a conventional online fashion marketplace.
paragraph3: HeyDoc AI Founded In: 2020 Founders: Mrinal Tyagi, Navneet Tyagi Headquarters: Mandi HeyDoc AI offers AI-powered solutions for hospitals, healthcare providers, and public health systems that automate patient interactions, clinical workflows, appointment management and care coordination. The startup also offers WellnessGPT, an enterprise AI platform that provides clinically aligned virtual assistants for patients and healthcare professionals. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU Kisanwala Founded In: 2020 Founders: Suresh Atluri, Parag Modi Headquarters: Hyderabad The AI-based agritech platform helps farmers improve productivity and income via an integrated suite of digital agriculture solutions. The platform offers premium agri-inputs such as seeds and crop protection products, on-demand farm machinery rentals, commodity price forecasting, crop advisory, agronomy services, soil testing, and financial advisory. Lingopanda (formerly PingoLearn) Founded In: 2021 Founders: Shubham Maheshwari, Mohit Menghani Headquarters: Bengaluru Lingopanda is an AI-powered language learning platform focused on helping users improve their spoken English and other language skills through conversation-based learning. The app focuses on interactive role-play scenarios, bite-sized video content, pronunciation practice and AI-driven speech feedback to help learners engage in real-world conversations. LUZO Founded In: 2021 Founders: Anurav Dave, Nikhil Kalwani, Maan Jetley Headquarters: Mumbai The beauty and wellness marketplace enables users to discover, compare and book appointments at premium salons, spas, and dermatology clinics via a mobile app. It offers users curated recommendations to access premium grooming and wellness services more conveniently.
paragraph4: Machaxi Founded In: 2019 Founders: Pratish Raj, Tushar Raj, Ashish Anand Headquarters: Bengaluru Machaxi is a sports tech platform that enables users to discover, book, and participate in sports activities through a membership-based model. The platform offers access to partner sports centres, coaching programmes, and sports equipment, allowing users to play multiple sports such as badminton, football, cricket, swimming, table tennis, and more through a single app. MetaShot Founded In: 2021 Founders: Prince Thomas, Ranjit Behera, Ajith Sunny Headquarters: Bengaluru The mixed reality gaming startup develops motion-enabled gaming hardware and software to bring real-world sports into the living room. Its flagship product is a smart cricket bat embedded with motion sensors that replicates a player’s physical shots inside a virtual cricket game, allowing users to play on smartphones, smart TVs, laptops, and tablets. MindYourLogic Studios Founded In: 2018 Founders: Anshul Khandelwal Headquarters: Nagpur MindYourLogic Studios creates games, animations, books, and digital content designed to improve logical reasoning, problem-solving, and critical thinking. The startup produces brain-training games, detective stories, riddles, puzzles, and educational animations that are distributed across mobile apps, YouTube channels and other digital platforms. MrMed Founded In: 2020 Founders: Devashish Singh, Saurab Jain Headquarters: Chennai MrMed operates as a specialised online pharmacy focused on medicines for patients with chronic and life-threatening conditions such as cancer, kidney disease, heart disorders, HIV/AIDS and organ transplants. In addition to medicine delivery, MrMed offers services such as patient assistance programmes (PAPs), import of specialty medicines, cold-chain logistics for temperature-sensitive drugs, medication counselling and adherence support.
paragraph5: Plutus Labs Founded In: 2021 Founders: Karata Dasmahapatra, Shivanshu Tyagi, Sambhav Jain Headquarters: Delhi NCR Plutus Labs combines AI-generated game creation, social interaction, and creator monetisation into a single platform. It allows creators to host live games, quizzes, and community challenges, helping them engage fans while generating revenue through paid participation, rewards, and virtual experiences. Regain Founded In: 2023 Founders: Ahmed Nizam Mohaideen Headquarters: Bengaluru Regain is an AI-powered digital wellbeing and productivity app that helps users reduce smartphone distractions and improve focus. It offers features such as strict mode, study mode, focus timers, app usage analytics, and personalised productivity insights, helping users to block distracting apps and websites, limit social media usage and schedule focus sessions.

title_bn: Omspace is building a reusable rocket in Ahmedabad for small satellite launches
author: TechPulse

title: New HBF spec outlines tech that can give GPUs terabytes of extra memory — Sandisk and SK hynix unveil spec with up to 16-Hi NAND stacks, 3 TB/s bandwidth, UCIe
title_bn: New HBF spec outlines tech that can give GPUs terabytes of extra memory — Sandisk and SK hynix unveil spec with up to 16-Hi NAND stacks, 3 TB/s bandwidth, UCIe
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Sandisk and SK hynix formally introduce HBF specification that promises up to 3 TB/s of bandwidth eventually, though only four companies are currently interested in the technology.
paragraph1: (Image credit: SanDisk) Sandisk and SK hynix on Tuesday formally introduced the High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) specification, their jointly developed storage technology that promises to bring together the non-volatility of 3D NAND and the performance of High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), which will be handy for AI inference systems. The specification was released through the Open Compute Project (OCP), so it will be an open standard rather than a proprietary interface.Tom's Hardware Premium RoadmapsThe initial specification defines HBF packages with capacities of up to 512GB using either 8-Hi or 16-Hi NAND die stacks, though these will not be standard 3D NAND stacks, but rather specialized devices with a fast interface. In fact, Sandisk once called them HBF core dies rather than 3D NAND die stacks.Performance of HBF is divided into three bandwidth grades ranging from approximately 0.4 TB/s to 3.
paragraph2: 0 TB/s (though we are not sure whether this figure describes the full HBF subsystem or per-package bandwidth). Such a huge performance range implies that Sandisk and SK hynix expect HBF to have a multi-year roadmap featuring multiple implementations and generations of HBF. It is noteworthy that the most capable implementation of HBF (3 TB/s) is set to beat the memory bandwidth of a single HBM4 memory stack (2 TB/s), though it will be unlikely to beat HBM4 when it comes to latency. (Image credit: SanDisk)Interestingly, SK hynix claims that HBF uses the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) standard to simplify integration with heterogeneous computing platforms, whereas Sandisk claims that HBF is set to adopt the 'xPU-HBF' interface, which could be its definition of UCIe implemented by companies like Broadcom or Marvell.In addition to capacity and performance targets, the specification establishes electrical and interface characteristics, packaging and reliability guidelines for stacked HBF devices, as well as software I/O requirements. For now, these specifications are not officially published by the OCP.
paragraph3: (Image credit: SanDisk)Extracting 400 GB/s of bandwidth from a single 512GB HBF package is not a trivial task. To enable such a package, Sandisk once planned to use 16 HBF core dies that feature many, many arrays that can be accessed concurrently using dedicated read/write paths. Meanwhile, it is possible to reach over 400 GB/s of bandwidth per package using a single UCIe interface that runs at up to 64 GT/s and features 64 lanes. Yet, this means that the HBF base die will be a fairly complex piece of silicon.Sandisk and SK hynix position HBF as a new memory tier for AI inference workloads by combining near-memory bandwidth with the higher capacity and non-volatility of NAND flash. The technology is aimed at workloads that require substantially larger memory pools close to compute than HBM alone can economically provide.
paragraph4: For example, while the maximum capacity of an HBM4 stack is 64GB, an HBF stack can provide up to 512GB. Even at a lower bandwidth, such memory can be useful for inference workloads.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Arguably the biggest question about HBF is who is going to adopt the technology? Since Sandisk and SK hynix announced plans to collaborate on defining the HBF specification in 2025, only Google and Tenstorrent have expressed interest in participating in the HBF consortium. Meanwhile, AMD, Broadcom, Intel, Nvidia, Marvell, Micron, Qualcomm, Samsung, and Western Digital have so far expressed no interest in HBF.
paragraph5: Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds. Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

title: Apple crosses $10 billion in India sales on widening retail push
title_bn: Apple crosses $10 billion in India sales on widening retail push
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple Inc. exceeded $10 billion in annual sales in India for the first time last fiscal year, underscoring surging demand for its pricey devices in a market where it’s steadily ramping up its retail network.
paragraph1: Apple Inc. exceeded $10 billion in annual sales in India for the first time last fiscal year, underscoring surging demand for its pricey devices in a market where it’s steadily ramping up its retail network.Apple Surpasses $10 Billion in Annual Sales in India Amid Growing Demand(REUTERS)Apple Inc. exceeded $10 billion in annual sales in India for the first time last fiscal year, underscoring surging demand for its pricey devices in a market where it’s steadily ramping up its retail network.Revenue grew at double-digit percentage rate in the 12 months through March from about $9 billion a year earlier, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified as the information is private. Apple’s marquee iPhones accounted for a significant majority of the sales, while demand for iPads and MacBooks also rose, the person said.
paragraph2: The previously unreported figures in the world’s most populous country are a boon for Apple’s efforts to find new growth markets. While India still represents just a fraction of its overall business, the South Asian country is emerging as one of its key sales regions outside of the US and China.Apple representatives didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.India could further gain in significance given the US’s increasingly uneasy geopolitical relationship with China, which is the Cupertino, California-based company’s largest overseas market. Apple’s latest quarterly sales in China amounted to $18.8 billion, short of the $19.
paragraph3: 6 billion estimated by some analysts. It’s also a market where local smartphone rivals such as Huawei Technologies Co. often outsell Apple.Apple’s recent sales figures from India, when presented in US dollars, are diminished by the rupee’s decline. The Indian currency has dropped about 10% against the greenback since the start of last year.As part of its India retail expansion, Apple opened a new store in the financial capital of Mumbai in February, taking its official shop count in the country to six.
paragraph4: India’s local sourcing requirements kept Apple away from opening its iconic stores in the South Asian nation for years. As the policy eased, Apple finally launched its online store in India in 2020. Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook then inaugurated the first two stores in India, respectively located in Mumbai and New Delhi, in 2023. The company has since boosted its retail network in the country and added more premium resellers.High taxes make iPhones pricey in India — Apple sells the entry-level iPhone 17 model at 82,900 rupees ($870) in India, compared with the $799 price tag in the US, where it also leases the device for as little as $23 a month. To grow its market share the company has partnered with banks for credit card rebates, and also offers student discounts and trade-ins on older devices.
paragraph5: Cook has consistently said India is among the company’s fastest-growing markets.India has also become key to Apple’s manufacturing strategy, with five factories producing iPhones. One in every four iPhones is now made in India, and it’s the major source of US-bound devices.

title: ET Now Acquires OpiGo To Expand Its Investment Platform
title_bn: ET Now Acquires OpiGo To Expand Its Investment Platform
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Media giant Times Network has acquired fintech startup OpiGo for an undisclosed amount as part of ET NOW’s expansion into…
paragraph1: SUMMARYMedia giant Times Network has acquired fintech startup OpiGo for an undisclosed amount as part of ET NOW’s expansion into investor-focused financial services The deal is in line with a wider shift in India’s financial services market, where brands have increasingly looked to monetise their audiences through advisory, community, and subscription-led products OpiGo’s acquisition helps ET NOW Pro bring live trade ideas, recommendations from SEBI-registered research analysts, investor communities, premium financial content, market insights, and access to its Pay TV channel under one offering Media giant Times Network has acquired fintech startup OpiGo for an undisclosed amount as part of ET NOW’s expansion into investor-focused financial services. With the acquisition, OpiGo’s platform, which helped retail investors better understand their investment thesis, will be integrated within its premium investor subscription platform, ET NOW Pro. Founded in 2022 by Devansh Mehta, OpiGo provides stock recommendations from SEBI-registered experts, giving insights into short-term trades, long-term investments, and industries or sectors.
paragraph2: The platform provides investors access to community-driven opinions on various stocks. The fintech startup has raised a pre-seed funding round of $168K (₹1.4 Cr) in 2024 from angel investors including Shubham Satyarth and Manish Choksi.
paragraph3: OpiGo’s acquisition helps ET NOW Pro bring live trade ideas, recommendations from SEBI-registered research analysts, investor communities, premium financial content, market insights, and access to its Pay TV channel under one offering. Launched in 2023, ET Now is a digital business news platform. Post the merger, it will expand beyond business news into a broader financial intelligence and investor engagement platform.
paragraph4: The app also gives a thorough breakdown of critical investment information like price to earnings, price to book, return on equity, revenues, profit/loss, among others. “Joining forces with ET NOW will scale this vision significantly and create a trusted destination where investors can seamlessly access quality content, expert research and investing tools within one integrated ecosystem,” OpiGo’s Mehta said. The deal is in line with a wider shift in India’s financial services market, where brands have increasingly looked to monetise their audiences through advisory, community, and subscription-led products.
paragraph5: India’s fintech sector has also seen stronger demand for compliance-first investing platforms as SEBI tightened oversight of research analysts and investment advisors.

author: TechPulse
excerpt: WhatsApp today announced a series of updates to group chats, including an "@all" mention feature, three new poll upgrades, and a faster way to spin off new groups from existing ones. The most notable addition is @all, which lets a group member alert
paragraph1: WhatsApp today announced a series of updates to group chats, including an "@all" mention feature, three new poll upgrades, and a faster way to spin off new groups from existing ones. The most notable addition is @all, which lets a group member alert everyone in a chat at once instead of tagging people individually. WhatsApp says the feature is meant for important, time-sensitive messages, such as school or office closures, event deadlines, or last-minute changes to plans. In groups with more than 32 members, only admins can use @all. The mention will surface even in muted chats, though WhatsApp says users can mute @all specifically in their notification settings if they want to opt out.
paragraph2: Polls are also gaining three improvements. Poll creators can now set an end time that automatically locks voting once it passes, hide voter names so participants can respond without others seeing their choices, and edit a poll's question for up to 15 minutes after posting it to fix typos or add clarity. WhatsApp is also simplifying group creation. A new "Create a similar group" option lets users start a new group chat populated with members from an existing one in a single tap, rather than adding participants one by one. WhatsApp suggests the feature for splitting off side conversations, such as planning a surprise party away from the group being surprised, or diving into a specific topic without cluttering the main chat.
paragraph3: Today's changes come as a continuation of updates introduced earlier this year, when WhatsApp added group message history, member tags, and event reminders. WhatsApp has more than 100 million users in the U.S. and over 3 billion globally. title: OpenAI says Apple's trade secrets lawsuit is "aggressive and oddly personal"
title_bn: OpenAI says Apple's trade secrets lawsuit is "aggressive and oddly personal"
author: TechPulse
excerpt: “We do not have, nor want, any of their trade secrets,” the ChatGPT maker says.
paragraph1: The start-up said Apple “never raised the specific allegations in this lawsuit at that time” and “in fact told us that they were ‘resolving any issues.’ We then heard nothing for five months until they sued.” Apple alleged in its lawsuit that Chang Liu, a former employee who worked on some of its “most sensitive product development programs,” accessed Apple’s trade secrets after leaving the company in January.
paragraph2: However OpenAI said Apple employees had themselves contacted Liu “and asked for his help to locate this information,” something the iPhone maker “only now admits.” Apple also named in its lawsuit a second former employee, OpenAI’s chief hardware officer, Tang Tan, whom it accused of seeking out proprietary information when interviewing Apple’s employees. “Tang has always been clear with the team that we do not want, and must not use, any confidential information from other companies,” wrote OpenAI.
paragraph3: Apple on Monday sought a preliminary injunction in the US to prevent former employees and OpenAI from accessing, using, or disclosing its trade secrets. It also filed a second motion asking the court to expedite discovery and order several OpenAI employees, including Liu and Tan, to sit for depositions. OpenAI said Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction was “both based on false information and completely unnecessary because we do not have, nor want, any of their trade secrets.
paragraph4: ” “Apple is one of the greatest companies of all time, and built a reputation for obsessing over the smallest details. This careless, aggressive and oddly personal lawsuit sadly doesn’t live up to that reputation,” the ChatGPT maker wrote. Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

paragraph2: Other backers include A16z, Base10 and Y Combinator, as well as strategic investors T.Capital, Orange and Endeavor Catalyst.The round brings the total funding raised by European AI agent startups this year to more than €7.
paragraph3: 85bn, surpassing last year's full-year total of €6.2bn, according to Sifted data.HappyRobot helps enterprises build, deploy and manage AI agents across complex workflows.
paragraph4: It currently works with over 150 businesses, including DHL and Uber. title: How Octobotics Is Saving Human Lives By Placing Robots In Hazardous Industrial Jobs
title_bn: How Octobotics Is Saving Human Lives By Placing Robots In Hazardous Industrial Jobs
author: TechPulse
excerpt: In July 2025, two field operators working with Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) died after they were exposed to…
paragraph1: SUMMARYDelhi NCR-based deeptech startup Octobotics is scaling its robotic industrial inspection business with lighter modular robots, a services-first model, and fresh seed funding to replace hazardous manual inspections. As industries face growing pressure to improve worker safety and infrastructure maintenance, robotic inspections could reduce fatalities, cut inspection time, and modernise a traditionally manual sector. Founded in 2020, Octobotics builds magnetic crawler robots that use phased-array ultrasonic testing to detect structural defects and serves clients including IOCL and BPCL. In July 2025, two field operators working with Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) died after they were exposed to hazardous vapours while investigating a malfunction in a storage tank. This is the morbid reality that many face during regular inspections. And this barely scrapes the surface. From a ship’s ballast compartments to offshore structures, inspection workers often face other significant risks too – falls, exposure to toxic gases and oxygen-deficient environments. Having witnessed several casualties during industrial inspections, Ishan Bhatnagar and Gulshan Kumar decided that it was time to put a stop to these life-claiming incidents. They banded together and started Octobotics in 2020 to solve this problem. Headquartered in Delhi NCR, Octobotics has built magnetic crawler robots that can climb steel structures, operate ultrasonic sensors across surfaces and generate inspection reports. “We watched people risk their lives and sometimes lose them, just to determine whether a ship, tank or pipeline was safe. We believed a robot should be doing that job instead,” said Octobotics founder Bhatnagar. In the five years since its inception, the startup has built two prototypes that cater to a wide gamut of sectors, such as oil and gas, marine and railways.
paragraph2: It recently also raised ₹10 Cr in its seed funding round from Navam Capital and BYT Capital. From Dorms To Robots Bhatnagar and Kumar shared a dorm room while studying engineering at the Marine Engineering and Research Institute, Kolkata. They eventually graduated and went their separate ways into offshore careers. In 2014, Bhatnagar was working with a Norwegian oil and gas company as an engineer, overseeing the operations of very large crude carriers (VLCCs). Gulshan, meanwhile, was working as an engineer with a Belgian company, DEME Group, a contractor for offshore energy, dredging and marine infrastructure. By the mid-2010s, both were in mid-management roles, earning upwards of $10,000 a month. The work took them to rigs, vessels, and industrial plants across the world. And it showed them, repeatedly, what happened when inspections went wrong. “In 2017, someone fell from a height of 40 meters, and their head opened up,” Bhatnagar recalled. In 2020, they left their jobs, pooled their savings, and incorporated Octobotics. Initially, the cofounders experimented with aerial inspection. The duo built a drone-based inspection platform, carrying cameras and sensors, which hovered alongside steel structures to scan them from a distance. While the hypothesis was reasonable as drones were becoming cheaper and more capable, the plan didn’t work.
paragraph3: The real breakthrough came a year later in 2021, when the two built their prototype – a magnetic crawler robot. The same year, Octobotics filed its first patent on a robotic arm design, and it was eventually granted. Two more patents followed, both covering applications of non-destructive testing technology in railways and oil and gas. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU The startup today holds three granted patents, with two more under review and three additional filings planned in the coming months. But what are these patents powering? The Tech Of Listening To Steel The startup has two major products in its portfolio: a magnetic crawler robot and a ten-metre pole-mounted inspection system called ReachMaster. Octobotics’ robot uses magnetic adhesion to grip steel surfaces, crawl across them and press ultrasonic sensors directly against the material to detect cracks, corrosion and internal defects. In line with this, most may think that the startup’s edge lies in hardware. But Bhatnagar says that Octobotics’ expertise sits well at the intersection of metallurgy, non-destructive testing (NDT), software engineering and robotics. For context, NDT is the art of evaluating the integrity or defects of a structure without altering its original use. At the heart of Octobotics’ tech stack is phased array ultrasonics, which works on the same premise as a medical ultrasound. Sound waves are sent into a material, and when they hit a defect, they reflect. The system reads those reflections and maps what lies beneath the surface.
paragraph4: But unlike a standard ultrasound that sends a single wave, a phased array can send waves with multiple channels simultaneously at controlled angles. This produces a detailed picture of cracks, corrosion and other defects, allowing Octobotics to pinpoint their location, size and depth. The startup’s tech stack does not merely stop at hardware, it extends to software as well. Octobotics also uses test samples, with defects of known sizes and locations, to train its robots. By analysing the ultrasonic signals, the software learns to identify the presence, location and severity of defects with increasing accuracy. This forms the core of the robot’s training and development process. Having cracked the hardware, the deeptech startup is now moving to its next phase of execution and debuting new products. The Modular Inspection Layer Octobotics initially sold its robots in two separate variants. While the Weld Sensei was built for weld inspection, the Track Sensei catered to ultrasonic testing (UT) gridding (measuring defects and corrosion across metal surfaces like pipes and storage tanks). But it is now phasing out these robots for newer products. “We received strong feedback from customers that our previous-generation robots were too heavy, weighing around 37 kg on average,” Bhatnagar added. The startup is now working on a single modular platform under 15 kilograms, which can carry both inspection technologies (weld and UT gridding) through interchangeable modules. The new models are set to debut around August 15th, and will focus on India and the Middle East as the initial focus markets.
paragraph5: Speaking about its clientele, Octobotics claims to have eight commercial enterprises under its belt spanning three sectors. These include Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), among others. However, half of its revenue still comes from companies in overseas markets like Singapore, Greece, and the Middle East. Ahead of the launch of its new offerings, the startup has now also pivoted to a service-based revenue model. Under this, Octobotics deploys two field teams, each equipped with a robot, and charges customers on a per-inspection basis. A typical storage tank inspection costs around ₹10 Lakh and is completed in about two days, compared to nearly ten days using conventional manual methods. For more complex assets such as refinery cracker units, inspection contracts can generate ₹20 Lakh to ₹25 Lakh per job. However, Octobotics aspires to move towards a distribution model where robots are rented to third-party vendors who conduct inspections independently. It also plans to pair its hardware with a SaaS reporting layer to bring an additional stream of revenue. Nevertheless, the Delhi-NCR-based startup continues to see healthy traction. It closed FY26 with revenues of ₹1.94 Cr, with a target of hitting ₹6 Cr in top line in the ongoing fiscal year (FY27). While the target is not small by any means, the startup is banking on its hardware-first, service playbook to offer faster and affordable inspections for large industrial giants.

title: Nothing launches CMF Clip Pro to fix open-ear audio’s biggest flaws
title_bn: Nothing launches CMF Clip Pro to fix open-ear audio’s biggest flaws
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Priced at £79, the earbuds feature a 3-point clip structure, custom bass technology, and an app-controlled sound seal system.
paragraph1: TL;DR Nothing has launched the new CMF Clip Pro under its CMF sub-brand for just $99. The CMF Clip Pro open-ear earbuds weigh 6.5g each and use a three-point clip structure with a flexible 0.5mm titanium wire C-bridge to eliminate wearing fatigue. Other notable features include a rotatable and customizable Smart Dial on the case, LDAC support, and an app-controlled Sound Seal system to minimize audio leakage. Nothing was reportedly said to be shifting to an AI-first strategy, with wearables and audio products taking priority over smartphones in a phased rollout. While the company didn’t comment on the report, Nothing’s CMF sub-brand has now officially announced the CMF Clip Pro, an open-ear earbud that marks the company’s entry into the increasingly crowded open-ear audio race.
paragraph2: With the CMF Clip Pro, Nothing is tackling the real-world problems of wearing fatigue and sound quality that plague open-ear earbuds. The Clip Pro utilizes a distinctive three-point clip design that distributes clamping pressure across three contact points on the ear rather than focusing it on a single spot. The structure features a flexible titanium wire C-bridge wrapped in skin-friendly TPU, which Nothing says contours to virtually any ear shape.With a weight of just 6.5g per earbud and a tiny 13.8mm listening ball, the hardware is designed to effectively “disappear” during all-day use.Open-ear earbuds notoriously suffer from weak bass response, but CMF has packed a customized 10.
paragraph3: 8mm dual-magnet dynamic driver into the Clip Pro. title: EU’s €5bn tech superfund officially open for business
title_bn: EU’s €5bn tech superfund officially open for business
author: TechPulse
paragraph1: After roughly a year of planning, speculating and negotiating, the European Commission’s €5bn Scaleup Europe Fund is ready to invest, with its first deals expected in the coming weeks. The Commission announced on Tuesday that the fund, run by Swedish investment firm EQT, completed all legal proceedings and will finally start investing after months of chatter over which companies it will back.
paragraph2: “From today, [the Scaleup Europe Fund] will ensure our scaleups can find what they need right here in Europe to grow into world-leading companies,” European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen said in a statement. Sifted recently reported the fund was in talks to lead or co-lead a fresh funding round for French AI titan Mistral, which is said to be targeting €3bn in new capital.
paragraph3: The Scaleup fund has also reportedly been in talks with Franco-German spacetech The Exploration Company for its new round, which Sifted understands could be around $350m; EQT declined to comment. EQT previously told Sifted that it has a pipeline of over 100 startups.
paragraph4: It will typically lead or co-lead investments of between €100m-500m. EQT is still helping fundraise the remainder of the €5bn target; existing LPs include Novo Holdings, EIFO (the Export and Investment Fund of Denmark), Santander/Mouro Capital, APG Asset Management on behalf of Dutch pension fund ABP, Wallenberg Investments and Allianz.
paragraph5: Sifted recently reported that the UK was also in talks to invest in the Scaleup fund via the British Business Bank, although the French government has pushed back.

title: HappyRobot lands $150M Series C to scale agentic AI for enterprise operations
title_bn: HappyRobot lands $150M Series C to scale agentic AI for enterprise operations
author: TechPulse
excerpt: HappyRobot, a company developing agentic AI for supply chains has raised $150 million in Series C funding led by Prysm Capital and co-led by Eurazeo. Existing investors a16z, Base10, Y Combinator are ...
paragraph1: HappyRobot, a company developing agentic AI for supply chains has raised $150 million in Series C funding led by Prysm Capital and co-led by Eurazeo. Existing investors a16z, Base10, Y Combinator are doubling down with participation from strategics like Koch Disruptive Technologies (KDT), KFund, Orange, and T.Capital (Deutsche Telekom), Bankinter, Endeavor Catalyst and Wave-X. The round values the company at $1.2 billion post-money, bringing total funding to around $200 million. Enterprise operations continue to rely on millions of phone calls, emails, documents and disconnected systems every day.
paragraph2: While AI has made it easier to generate information, many organisations still struggle to automate the work required to keep their businesses running. HappyRobot bridges that gap by deploying AI agents that can execute and reason within existing enterprise systems while working alongside employees. HappyRobot’s platform enables organisations to build, deploy, and manage AI agents that automate complex operational workflows across voice, email, documents, and the web. By learning from every interaction and execution, it helps organisations capture operational knowledge, streamline information exchange, and gain real-time visibility across their operations. Through the millions of tasks HappyRobot agents execute each month, customers are seeing measurable impact across departments. Deployment isn't a one-time project but an ongoing partnership: initial agents typically go live within 4 to 12 weeks, and each sprint that follows refines the agents already in production and adds new ones.
paragraph3: One customer is automating 28,000 hours of work every month. In customer care, agents are achieving 9.4/10 customer satisfaction scores and more than 70 per cent autonomous resolution on average. Operational teams have increased capacity by 10x, and sales teams have generated 5x more revenue through previously underutilised channels. The company works with more than 150+ enterprise customers, including DHL, Kuehne + Nagel, Naturgy, Repsol, and Uber, and has grown 5x since raising its Series B late last year. After first proving its platform in logistics, one of the world’s most operationally demanding industries, HappyRobot is expanding across the supply chain as well as into insurance, energy and utilities, telecommunications, airlines, and other sectors where business-critical work still depends on manual coordination across fragmented systems.
paragraph4: “Getting agents to do work is the starting point, not the destination,” said Pablo Palafox, co-founder and CEO of HappyRobot. “HappyRobot's thesis is that enterprise superintelligence, where an organisation's collective intelligence compounds as agents and people learn from one another, requires far more than task-performing agents. It requires a platform and a deployed motion capable of operationalising that platform inside a specific business.” “Many industries have a surprising share of their costs locked up in coordination, the calls, emails, and handoffs that keep work flowing,” said Kerry Wei, Partner at Prysm Capital “While getting an agent to complete a discrete task is increasingly simple, deploying them across multi-step enterprise workflows has proven far more difficult. HappyRobot has built the missing link – the governance, interfaces, and context layer – that enables agents to work seamlessly across complex workflows, driving real ROI by allowing companies to capture value without asking employees to adopt anything new.” "It had been a while since we met a company that fundamentally expands what enterprise AI can do,” said Anne-Charlotte Philbert, Partner at Eurazeo: “From day one, we knew Pablo and the team were building something special: a truly AI-native platform, world-class technical depth, and customers seeing exceptional ROI in mission-critical industries such as supply chain, energy, telecommunications, and banking."
paragraph5: Over the past year, HappyRobot has expanded from two offices to eight locations across North America, Europe, LATAM, and Australia, reflecting growing demand from enterprises looking to automate complex operational workflows. The new funding will accelerate investment in HappyRobot’s platform, including expanded AI capabilities, enterprise integrations and the infrastructure required to deploy AI agents at scale. The company will also continue growing its engineering, deployment and go-to-market teams globally to support increasing demand from enterprises across industries.

title: OpenAI Posts Public Rebuttal to Apple's Trade Secrets Lawsuit
title_bn: OpenAI Posts Public Rebuttal to Apple's Trade Secrets Lawsuit
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple has asked a federal judge for a preliminary injunction against OpenAI as its trade secrets lawsuit escalates, and OpenAI responded hours later with a detailed public rebuttal that includes internal messages and legal correspondence. Reuters rep
paragraph1: Apple has asked a federal judge for a preliminary injunction against OpenAI as its trade secrets lawsuit escalates, and OpenAI responded hours later with a detailed public rebuttal that includes internal messages and legal correspondence. Reuters reports that Apple yesterday filed a motion seeking to bar OpenAI and two former employees, Chang Liu and Tang Tan, from accessing, using, or disclosing its alleged confidential information, along with a request for expedited discovery. "Apple will be irreparably harmed absent a preliminary injunction," the company said in its filing. Apple originally sued OpenAI on July 10, alleging that former Apple engineer Liu and former Apple design executive Tan ran a scheme to funnel confidential product information to OpenAI's hardware business. OpenAI has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing, saying it has "no interest in other companies' trade secrets."
paragraph2: Late on Monday evening, OpenAI published a blog post titled "Apple is getting this wrong," calling the lawsuit "careless, aggressive and oddly personal." The company disputes Apple's account of its pre-litigation contact, saying Apple's outside counsel emailed the wrong person in February after confusing two Asian last names, and published the underlying email chain showing the mix-up, along with an apology from Apple's counsel. OpenAI says it heard nothing further about the specific allegations for five months before Apple filed suit. OpenAI published iMessage exchanges it says show Apple employees repeatedly asking Liu for help locating files and technical information after his January 22 departure, including directing a colleague to AirDrop files from his Apple-linked iCloud account. The same messages show an Apple employee still asking Liu about internal files as late as March 5, with another participant in the thread calling the exchange "highly irregular."
paragraph3: OpenAI also defended Tan, who spent 24 years at Apple before joining io Products, the hardware startup he co-founded with Jony Ive, which merged with OpenAI in July 2025. "Tang has always been clear with the team that we do not want, and must not use, any confidential information from other companies," OpenAI said. Apple's complaint claims more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI. A hearing on Apple's injunction request has not yet been scheduled. title: A less powerful Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip is now officially a thing
title_bn: A less powerful Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip is now officially a thing
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5V aims to provide a balance of performance and cost savings.
paragraph1: QualcommTL;DR A prominent leaker has revealed key details about the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5V chipset that will debut on the Redmi K100 Pro in China next week. The cost-effective chipset will reportedly offer CPU performance on par with other 8 Elite Gen 5 versions, but with a slightly underpowered GPU. Given the rising component costs, this cost-effective Qualcomm chip may be the preferred choice for phone makers. The global RAM crisis has already forced smartphone manufacturers to bump up prices, and there are no signs of the trend abating anytime soon. In the meantime, we’ve learned that chipmaker Qualcomm is developing a cost-effective version of the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5.
paragraph2: Well, the first phone featuring this SoC is about to launch in China next week, and we’re gaining some early insight into its performance.Popular leaker Digital Chat Station shared some insights about the unreleased phone and its chipset on Weibo. For starters, this chip, known as the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5V (SM8850-1-AB), appears to be built using the same TSMC N3P manufacturing process as other 8 Elite Gen 5 models. It also retains high-performance 4.6GHz Oryon CPU cores.
paragraph3: These attributes mean the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5V will retain the raw CPU performance of its more expensive siblings. There are some changes in the graphics department, though, with the source noting that the Adreno 840 GPU included here is slightly underpowered.More specifically, the new chip offers the same sliced architecture as previous Elite chips, but appears to have only two slices. Furthermore, the GPU is said to have 12MB of dedicated graphics memory. By contrast, the full-blown Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 GPU has three slices and 18MB of dedicated graphics memory, while the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 GPU has two slices and no dedicated graphics memory.
paragraph4: Despite this apparent disadvantage, Digital Chat Station claims that games such as Honor of Kings, Delta Force, and Peacekeeper Elite maintained consistent frame rates. Meanwhile, titles like Genshin Impact reportedly experienced dips in frame rate during graphics-intensive activities.Separately, Redmi has shared benchmark scores for the new chipset and has previously revealed part of the K100 Pro’s hardware in teasers ahead of the August 11 launch. This is also how we know the upcoming smartphone will feature a 6.59-inch AMOLED screen with an impressive 185Hz refresh rate.
paragraph5: There’s also mention of a larger battery on the Redmi K100 Pro, though specific details haven’t been revealed just yet.While we don’t foresee this Redmi smartphone making its way to the US anytime soon, it signals an upcoming trend among phone makers as they try to cut costs. Consequently, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5V may continue to thrive even after Qualcomm releases the next generation of its high-end mobile SoCs, which could have steep prices.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

By contrast, the full-blown Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 GPU has three slices and 18MB of dedicated graphics memory, while the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 GPU has two slices and no dedicated graphics memory.
bangla_paragraph4: Despite this apparent disadvantage, Digital Chat Station claims that games such as Honor of Kings, Delta Force, and Peacekeeper Elite maintained consistent frame rates. Meanwhile, titles like Genshin Impact reportedly experienced dips in frame rate during graphics-intensive activities.Separately, Redmi has shared benchmark scores for the new chipset and has previously revealed part of the K100 Pro’s hardware in teasers ahead of the August 11 launch. This is also how we know the upcoming smartphone will feature a 6.59-inch AMOLED screen with an impressive 185Hz refresh rate.
bangla_paragraph5: There’s also mention of a larger battery on the Redmi K100 Pro, though specific details haven’t been revealed just yet.While we don’t foresee this Redmi smartphone making its way to the US anytime soon, it signals an upcoming trend among phone makers as they try to cut costs. Consequently, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5V may continue to thrive even after Qualcomm releases the next generation of its high-end mobile SoCs, which could have steep prices.FollowThank you for being part of our community. title: Sylvox vs Samsung The Terrace vs SunBrite: The outdoor TV comparison you need before buying!
title_bn: Sylvox vs Samsung The Terrace vs SunBrite: The outdoor TV comparison you need before buying!
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Transform your backyard into the perfect entertainment hub with one of these outdoor TVs.
paragraph1: Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityOutdoor TVs have gained popularity in recent years, but your options still aren’t as wide as with regular TVs. The main brands are still Sylvox, Samsung, and Sunbrite. Of course, only one of these brands is widely known, so it’s hard to decide which best fits your needs. How do you pick? After all, getting one of these represents a solid investment in your outdoor entertainment.Don’t you worry! You don’t have to go through trial and error or spend your hard-earned money without knowing which is the right match. These are very expensive, after all (especially Samsung ones). I am doing all the hard work for you and comparing three of the main brands and models. My yard seriously looks like a multi-screen outdoor theater! I have the 65-inch models of the Sylvox Cinema Series, Samsung’s The Terrace, and a Sunbrite Solis.Which one should earn a spot in your yard? Well, as always, it depends on your needs and what you prioritize. These are outdoor TVs, so design and build quality are among the most important factors when picking between them.
paragraph2: Can they survive living outside? How about a storm? You want to make sure your expensive TV can actually be outside 24/7/365. How much can the Sylvox Cinema Series handle? A little bit of history before we talk about the Cinema Series. I have lived with a Sylvox Gaming Series TV for about a year. It lived outside the whole time, through rain and even snow. It actually fell a few times, due to strong winds. It survived the whole time until a couple of months ago, when it fell straight into a sharp rock corner. Even then, the TV still works, it’s just that there is a bar of dead lighting on the right side. It’s about four inches wide. I’d say it went through plenty of torture before actually experiencing real damage.With all that in mind, I can tell you that Sylvox TVs are very sturdy, and this one feels just as rugged, with the same solid metal build. This is no regular aluminum. Sylvox uses a premium aluminum alloy made specifically for outdoor environments. It’s thick, strong metal more akin to solid steel. It looks and feels rugged. Additionally, it has an IP56 rating, which means it is dust-protected and has been tested against powerful water jets from all directions. Of course, regular rain should be fine, and in my experience, even snow. The operating temperature range is impressively good: -22 to 122 Fahrenheit.
paragraph3: What about the Samsung The Terrace? Samsung’s The Terrace is a bit of an odd one in this department. It is definitely the slimmest, best-looking TV with the smallest bezels out of the three. That said, it also looks like it won’t be as resistant to drops or random things hitting it. It’s still made of metal, but it feels thinner and not as solid. Samsung, as it always does, paid much more attention to aesthetics with this one.Things like dust, rain, or snow should be no issue. It is also rated IP56. If I were you, I would definitely use a sturdy wall mount with this one, though. A stand can lean and fall in strong winds (I know this firsthand).Operating temperatures are just as good, though. It works at temps between -22 and 122 Fahrenheit, which is identical to Sylvox’s TV.Sunbrite has the lowest ingress protection If you worry about water, Sunbrite has a clear disadvantage here. Not that it will get destroyed after a rain or two, but it has a lower IP55 rating. This simply means it has been tested to resist less powerful jets. I wouldn’t worry too much, as rain still isn’t as powerful as any water jets. At least not most of the time.That said, the TV does feel rugged. The metal and construction feel more solid than Samsung’s, and it’s made of sturdier metal. If you live in extreme weather, you might not want to pick this one either, especially if it gets really cold.
paragraph4: The Sunbrite Solis TV operates at temperatures between 32 and 122 degrees. This might not be an issue for many, but some of us live in places where it gets below freezing in the winter.Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityThe one thing I especially liked about the Sunbrite Solis is that it has physical control buttons on the actual TV. Neither of the other TVs has this feature. You absolutely need a remote or phone to use them.The winner?: It depends Different people value different things, and that is totally fair. This is why I am choosing two winners in this section. If you want something more rugged, the obvious option is Sylvox. If you want something that looks good, has a slimmer design, and don’t mind keeping the TV in a relatively safe spot, then Samsung is the winner. How about the picture and audio quality? Design, construction, build quality, and all those things go out the door if a TV doesn’t look and sound great. That is the whole point of them, after all: watching content. How does the Sylvox Cinema Series TV look and sound?Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityIn general terms, Sylvox definitely doesn’t disappoint. It looked great when I tested the gaming series, and I feel like the Cinema Series improved upon that. The 4K resolution is crisp, and the 120Hz refresh rate is smooth. It also has a response time of less than 8ms, which is still really good for TVs.The Helio QLED panel delivers vibrant, saturated colors, combining quantum dot technology with a cutting-edge Mini LED backlight system engineered specifically for outdoor viewing conditions, achieving a balance of pure blacks, ultra-high contrast ratio, and vibrant colors. For users seeking flagship-level outdoor picture performance, the Sylvox Cinema Pro Series also features Mini LED technology and delivers up to 5,000 nits of brightness.
paragraph5: The Sylvox Cinema Series delivers a solid viewing experience and great sound quality. It makes no sacrifices. In real-world use, the Cinema Series’ 2,000-nit brightness worked great. I was able to comfortably watch TV with no issues, even when the sun was high and strong.In terms of audio quality, we’re looking at two 30W speakers. It delivers really nice sound, and I had to lower the volume quite a bit to avoid disturbing neighbors in my small, quiet town. The sound is rich and full, which is still surprising for a TV.Samsung has great picture quality, but the audio is seriously disappointingEdgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityThe Terrace’s panel looks quite outstanding. Remember seeing those showroom TVs at your local tech stores? The ones that looked unreal? This one looks like that.It’s not just about crisp 4K resolution. The NEO QLED panel produces rich colors. The refresh rate looks very smooth, and brightness is also great, maxing out at 2,000 nits. The Quantum Matrix with Mini LED really brings that potential to life. It features Neo Quantum HDR+, and it works very well.

title: Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 Review: A good display meets a low-power RTX 5060
title_bn: Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 Review: A good display meets a low-power RTX 5060
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 pairs an RTX 5060, 144 Hz display, and excellent upgradeability with a comfortable keyboard, but its low-power GPU configuration and outdated CPU leave it struggling against rivals at the same price.
paragraph1: The Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 gets the basics right for an entry-level gaming laptop, but its gaming performance is compromised by a low-power GPU and aging processor. Rival systems deliver stronger gaming and productivity performance. Unless upgradeability is a top priority, most shoppers will find better overall value elsewhere. Pros +Decent display +Comfortable keyboard and touchpad +Solid upgradeability Cons -Underpowered RTX 5060 implementation -Short battery life Why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test. The Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 has the right idea to compete with the best budget gaming laptops: skip the flashy design extras and focus on the hardware that matters. Its RTX 5060 graphics, 144 Hz IPS display, solid keyboard, and generous internal upgrade options give budget-strapped gamers plenty to like on paper. The reality is that this configuration is compromised in the area that matters most: gaming performance. Its RTX 5060 is held back by a 65W power limit and the CPU is several generations old, allowing rival machines in the same price range to post stronger results. The LOQ is usable and practical, but at this price, it needs stronger performance to stand out.Design of the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 Aptly named, the LOQ Essentials 15 embraces a no-frills design. Aside from LOQ branding on the lid, there’s little here meant to catch the eye, which is fitting for a laptop that’s intended to deliver performance at the lowest possible cost. Lenovo reserves premium materials and styling for its Legion gaming laptops.Fortunately, the budget considerations are mostly aesthetic, as the LOQ’s plastic chassis feels solid and has the durability you’d expect for daily home or school use. Its 0.
paragraph2: 97-inch thick profile and 5.07-pound weight don’t make it a great traveling companion are in line with competing laptops like Acer's Nitro V 16S AI, Asus’ TUF Gaming F16, and MSI's Cyborg 15. The latter is the lightest in the group, at 4.36 pounds. Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Lenovo’s port selection is practical: one USB-C port (10 Gbps), two USB-A ports (5 Gbps), an audio jack, Ethernet, and HDMI. You won't get truly high-speed ports like USB4/Thunderbolt 4 at this price. The Intel AX203 Wi-Fi 6 card is another example of this laptop's economical focus, though it shouldn't hold users back. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 Specifications Swipe to scroll horizontally CPU Intel Core i7-13650HX Graphics Nvidia RTX 5060 (8GB GDDR7, 1,455 MHz boost, 65 W maximum graphics power) Memory 16GB DDR5-4800 RAM (1x 16GB) Storage 512GB SSD (WD PC SN5000S) Display 15.6-inch, 1920 x 1080, IPS, anti-glare, 144 Hz Networking Intel Wi-Fi 6 AX203, Bluetooth 5.4 Ports USB-C (10 Gbps), 2x USB-A (5 Gbps), audio, Ethernet, HDMI Camera 720p Battery 60 Wh Power Adapter 135 W (barrel connector) Operating System Windows 11 Home Dimensions (WxDxH) 14.22 x 10.06 x 0.97 inches (361 x 256 x 25 mm) Weight 5.07 pounds (2.3 kg) Price (as configured) $1,269.
paragraph3: 99 Gaming and Graphics on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11We evaluated the LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 with a Core i7-13650HX processor, RTX 5060 graphics (65W), and 16GB of single-channel DDR5-4800 RAM. The processor is several years old though still packs a punch, with six Performance cores.Playing 007 First Light at 1080p with medium lighting settings, post effects on, and DLSS set to balanced, the LOQ produced playable frame rates, ranging from the mid-50s to low-70s FPS depending on the scene. The experience was never poor, but it lacked the fluidity I expected from a laptop carrying Nvidia's latest midrange GPU.Our benchmark comparison lineup consists of Acer's Nitro V 16S AI (Ryzen 7 260, RTX 5060 85W, $1,299.99 when tested), Asus' TUF Gaming F16 (Core i7-14650HX, RTX 5050 115W, $1,199.99), and MSI's Cyborg 15 C13WE (Core i5-13420H, RTX 5050 70W, $1,219.99).Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Image 1 of 6 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Overall, the LOQ’s results were disappointing. With a 65W power limit, its RTX 5060 simply doesn't deliver the level of performance buyers might expect from the badge. It was routinely outperformed by the TUF Gaming F16 using an RTX 5050, while Acer's higher-powered RTX 5060 laptop also finished comfortably ahead. The result is a gaming laptop that works well enough but struggles to justify its price when similarly priced alternatives make better use of comparable hardware.In Shadow of the Tomb Raider at the Highest detail preset, the LOQ’s 88 FPS only outpaced the Cyborg (82 FPS), while the Asus (95 FPS) and Acer (98 FPS) both pulled ahead. This story repeated in Far Cry 6 – with 75 FPS, the LOQ trailed Acer (82 FPS) and Asus (90 FPS), though it was within a few FPS of those units in Red Dead Redemption 2.
paragraph4: The LOQ’s only real victory was Cyberpunk 2077, where it achieved 38 FPS, with the Acer (32 FPS) trailing. The LOQ was one of two laptops tested with Forza Horizon 3, where it predictably had no trouble outgunning the Cyborg, 58 FPS to 51 FPS.To stress-test gaming laptops, we run 15 loops of the Metro Exodus stress test at RTX settings to simulate half an hour of gaming. The LOQ demonstrated stable performance throughout the test, averaging 59.79 FPS without a variance of more than one FPS across runs. During the test, the Core i7-13650HX ran at an average frequency of 2.73 GHz while the RTX 5060 averaged 1,919 MHz.Productivity Performance on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11Our LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 is built around a Core i7-13650HX, 16GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Throughout our testing, the LOQ's outdated CPU struggled against the newer silicon in the competition, only consistently outpacing the Cyborg with its equally dated Core i5-13420H. In the multi-core portion of Geekbench, the LOQ's score of 11,300 was well behind the Ryzen 7 260-powered Acer (12,837) and couldn't touch the Core i7-14650HX-powered Asus (15,013). The Asus also dominated Handbrake, completing that test in 3 minutes and 33 seconds compared to the LOQ's 4:35.The LOQ's average speed of 136 MBps in our 25GB file transfer is abnormal, but it also occurred on other drive benchmarks, though I never noticed any issues in loading games. The drive is a WD PC SN5000S using QLC.Lenovo didn't cut too many corners with the LOQ's display. The 15.
paragraph5: 6-inch IPS panel pairs a smooth 144 Hz refresh rate with an anti-glare finish that minimizes reflections. title: ‘Apple is getting this wrong,’ says OpenAI — startup blasts iPhone maker over lawsuit alleging it stole confidential information through ex-Apple employees
title_bn: ‘Apple is getting this wrong,’ says OpenAI — startup blasts iPhone maker over lawsuit alleging it stole confidential information through ex-Apple employees
author: TechPulse
excerpt: OpenAI denies Apple's allegations in a blog post. The company claims that it doesn't have and even doesn't want its rivals trade secrets.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty / Alex Wroblewski) Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI in July, alleging that the latter stole trade secrets through former Apple employees. The startup has finally publicly responded to the lawsuit today, posting a blog post on its website titled, “Apple is getting this wrong.”“Apple is one of the greatest companies of all time, and built a reputation for obsessing over the smallest details. This careless, aggressive and oddly personal lawsuit sadly doesn’t live up to that reputation,” the company said in its blog post. It also added, “Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction is both based on false information and completely unnecessary because we do not have, nor want, any of their trade secrets.
paragraph2: ”The case names OpenAI technical staff Chang Liu, chief hardware officer Tang Tan, OpenAI, and io Products as defendants. Liu worked as a senior electrical engineer at Apple, while Tan was its former vice president of product design for the iPhone, AirPods, and the Apple Watch. Interestingly, io Products, which was acquired by OpenAI last year, was founded by Tan alongside former Apple Chief Design Officer Jony Ive and other former Apple heavyweights.The tech giant requested a preliminary injunction to stop the accused from accessing, acquiring, using, or disclosing the alleged stolen trade secrets. Cupertino said in its filing, “Apple will be irreparably harmed absent a preliminary injunction.
paragraph3: ”OpenAI publicly responded to this legal request through its blog post, pointing out that many of its allegations were actually based on miscommunications and false information, and that this move is completely unnecessary. But whether what the AI tech giant claims is true or not, its research and operations on consumer hardware would likely be impaired if the judge grants Apple’s request.Although OpenAI’s primary product is ChatGPT and its other LLM-powered services, it’s been rumored that it’s also working on AI-powered hardware. Its first product is expected to be some sort of portable smart speaker with built-in cameras and sensors. Although this isn’t an iPhone replacement, like the botched Humane AI Pin, some experts say this move threatens Apple’s standing as the biggest consumer electronics company on the planet.
paragraph4: This is especially true as it still lags behind other tech giants when it comes to artificial intelligence, even though AI enthusiasts love using Apple silicon with its Unified Memory architecture.Apple’s preliminary injunction is just the opening stages of what might be an epic showdown between two tech giants. It will likely take months (or even years) before this case reaches a judgment or a settlement, meaning a preliminary injunction will definitely have a massive impact on OpenAI’s hardware dreams.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. title: Thousands of SMEs tap into MSCA funding [Sponsored]
title_bn: Thousands of SMEs tap into MSCA funding [Sponsored]
author: TechPulse
excerpt: More than 2,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have participated in projects funded by the EU's Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) over the past five years, giving companies access to in...
paragraph1: More than 2,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have participated in projects funded by the EU's Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) over the past five years, giving companies access to international research networks and highly skilled researchers. In the last 30 years, the MSCA has supported the careers of excellent researchers from Europe and beyond, enabling them to pursue their ideas across academia and industry. Collaboration between universities and companies has been a fundamental part of the MSCA since its inception in 1996, and the involvement of Europe’s SMEs has grown ever since. Over the last five years, over 4,300 businesses took part in MSCA projects, and more than half of them were SMEs. Since 2014 – when the EU’s Horizon 2020 funding programme was launched – more than €1 billion in funding has supported the participation of over 8,500 private companies across more than 3,000 projects. To help companies get the most out of the doctoral training networks, postdoctoral fellowships and staff exchanges on offer, the MSCA has created a business hub page.
paragraph2: For example, it explains how SMEs can team up with academia to apply for MSCA Staff Exchange funding, which enables research and research support staff to move across countries, sectors, and disciplines, gaining experience and sharing expertise. SMEs can also reduce R&D costs and administrative effort by applying for an MSCA COFUND grant, which helps cover the cost of selecting, recruiting and training researchers. The recently launched Choose Europe for Science pilot further expands opportunities for organisations to recruit outstanding researchers into longer-term positions. The action supports projects where both academic and private sector organisations hire postdoctoral researchers with a view to offering employment beyond the project period. The idea is to also widen adoption of MSCA’s best practice in research, promoting high standards and good working conditions. The MSCA Doctoral Networks, which support doctoral training, offer SMEs an opportunity to collaborate with universities in seeking MSCA funding.
paragraph3: For every three educational establishments participating in the Doctoral Networks, there were almost two private sector organisations, according to data gathered from 2021 to 2023. MSCA sees the highest engagement in Staff Exchanges and Doctoral Networks, where around half of the organisations involved come from the non-academic sector. International networks Doctoral Networks must include members from at least three different countries, showing how a commitment to international mobility runs through the MSCA. Another example is the Postdoctoral Fellowships, where the mobility rules say that applicants should not have lived or worked in the beneficiary country for more than 12 months out of the 36 immediately before the call deadline. This international focus benefits SME partners because they get to participate in stronger international research networks. This means they get access to advanced technologies and specialised expertise, while at the same time it encourages greater collaboration, enabling SMEs to strengthen the skills of their teams.
paragraph4: International mobility is a core feature of the programme. Many researchers remain in Europe after their fellowship, helping to strengthen the continent's research and innovation ecosystem. One example is SERENADE, an MSCA-funded Doctoral Network coordinated by BSH Appliances in Spain. The project brings together universities and companies to train seven doctoral candidates working on technologies to reduce food waste, including sensor-equipped food containers and artificial intelligence (AI)-powered freshness analysis. The initiative is training doctoral candidates from academic institutions in Belgium, Germany and Italy, who are splitting their time between academic research and industry work with one of the companies partnering in the project. It aims to produce two innovations to tackle food waste: sustainable containers with sensors to monitor whether the food inside them is still fresh, and a portable food analyser that uses AI to examine the freshness of unpackaged products.
paragraph5: The networked approach of the project is more efficient in addressing the complex challenges required to achieve these goals, compared with solo efforts, according to Sergio Gomez Ortiz, head of product development shared services at BSH Group in Zaragoza, Spain. Revathy Gurusamy, an MSCA doctoral candidate who is working on SERENADE, says she chose the project partly because of the real-world impact it could have. Working at BSH Appliances, she sees the potential for her team’s smart food-monitoring devices to reach millions of households, directly contributing to reducing food waste on a global scale. As demand grows for closer collaboration between research and industry, the MSCA continues to provide companies with opportunities to engage with international talent and collaborative research.

title: Samsung follows LG in killing Smart TV apps that rent out your internet
title_bn: Samsung follows LG in killing Smart TV apps that rent out your internet
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The new policy blocks Smart TV apps from hijacking your home Wi-Fi.
paragraph1: C. Scott Brown / Android AuthorityTL;DR Security researchers discovered that popular Samsung TV apps (like Pac-Man) secretly contained residential proxy SDKs from data brokers like Bright Data. Samsung is officially banning proxy SDKs, halting new app submissions, and purging existing offending apps from its store. The enforcement follows LG’s similar crackdown after research revealed over 42% of webOS apps secretly shared home bandwidth. Samsung is cracking down on Smart TV apps that bundle residential proxy software after security researchers found the technology embedded in several popular gaming titles, including one the company had previously promoted as an Editor’s Choice recommendation.The company confirmed to TechCrunch that it has already blocked new Smart TV app submissions that include residential proxy functionality.
paragraph2: It is now rolling out stricter developer policies while working to remove existing apps containing the software.The move comes after Norwegian cybersecurity firm Mnemonic took a deep dive into Samsung’s Tizen platform, rooting a Smart TV to understand how residential proxy SDKs end up on consumer devices. Its investigation uncovered Bright Data’s SDK in several games, including Pac-Man, a title that had been surfaced through Samsung’s own recommendations.If you’re unfamiliar with residential proxies, they are services that route internet traffic through ordinary home internet connections. They have legitimate uses, including web data collection and bypassing internet restrictions, but they’ve also become a popular tool for cybercriminals looking to hide malicious activity behind residential IP addresses. That’s why their growing presence in consumer apps has drawn increasing scrutiny.
paragraph3: The good news is that the researchers didn’t find Samsung TVs automatically sharing their owners’ internet connections. Instead, the Bright Data SDK remained dormant unless remotely enabled by the app developer. At that point, users would see a consent prompt before the service could be activated. Once accepted, however, the proxy service continued running in the background even after the game itself had been closed.Arguably, the more concerning discovery wasn’t the SDK itself but how these apps are built. Mnemonic found that many Samsung TV apps function as lightweight shells that download much of their actual code from remote servers.
paragraph4: That’s great for developers, who can ship updates without waiting for app review, but it also creates a blind spot. Features can change after an app has already been approved, making it far more difficult for Samsung or any app store operator to verify what users are ultimately running on their devices.This isn’t just a Samsung problem, either. The researchers note that residential proxy software has appeared in Android apps, Android TV streaming boxes, digital picture frames, and other always-connected devices, underscoring how widespread the practice has become.Samsung’s policy change follows a series of industry moves against residential proxy networks. Last month, LG said (via KrebsonSecurity) it would ban residential proxy software from its Smart TV app store after separate research found the technology in a significant portion of its TV apps.
paragraph5: Around the same time, Google disrupted the NetNut residential proxy network, disabled the infrastructure that operated it, and updated Google Play Protect to automatically warn users about Android apps that contain the NetNut SDK. Google said millions of devices — including smart TVs and streaming boxes — had been enrolled into such networks, allowing attackers to route traffic through unsuspecting users’ home internet connections.If anything, Samsung’s latest policy suggests the industry is finally starting to respond.FollowThank you for being part of our community. title: Your Pixel’s lock screen may be about to get its biggest shortcut upgrade in years
title_bn: Your Pixel’s lock screen may be about to get its biggest shortcut upgrade in years
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Letting you launch apps directly from the lock screen.
paragraph1: Rita El Khoury / Android AuthorityTL;DR The lock screen on Pixel devices may soon allow users to add app shortcuts. While other Android brands let you add widgets to the lock screen, Pixels limit users to basic shortcuts such as flashlight and camera. Among Android OEMs, Samsung already lets users add app shortcuts to the lock screen. The lock screen on Pixel devices may currently seem limited compared to rival Android devices. Google currently lacks the option to add lock screen widgets that a host of others, seemingly inspired by iOS, have, and currently limits users to basic shortcuts placed at the bottom of the screen — unless you use an unofficial app to tap into hidden lock screen features. That could change soon, as Google seems to be testing an option that not only outpaces other Android rivals but also iOS.You’re reading an Authority Insights story.
paragraph2: Authority Insights brings you all the latest exclusive reports, app teardowns, leaks, and in-depth tech coverage from the Android Authority team that you won’t find anywhere else.With Android 17 QPR2 Beta 2, Google appears to be exploring the option to launch with fewer steps. author: TechPulse
excerpt: Beauty and personal care marketplace Nykaa’s board of directors has approved a 51% stake acquisition of D2C skincare brand Aminu…
paragraph1: SUMMARYNykaa will acquire a 51% stake in premium D2C skincare brand Aminu for up to ₹32 Cr, strengthening its house of brands portfolio The deal deepens Nykaa's push into the premium skincare segment while expanding its portfolio of owned beauty brands amid rising demand for high-end BPC products Founded in 2019, Aminu reported a revenue of ₹19.4 Cr revenue in FY26, 50% YoY from around ₹13 Cr earned in FY25 Beauty and personal care marketplace Nykaa’s board of directors has approved a 51% stake acquisition of D2C skincare brand Aminu for a cash consideration of up to ₹32 Cr. As per exchange filings, the transaction is expected to be completed by September 15. Founded in 2019 by Prachi Bhandari and Aman Mohunta, Aminu retails skincare products including serums, cleaners, sunscreen, masks, moisturisers and other body care products.
paragraph2: The startup also offers free skin consultation services. Its products are priced in a more premium category, a segment where Nykaa is trying to expand in. Apart from the seven year old business’ premium positioning, Nykaa also seeks to benefit from its strong R&D and omnichannel distribution capabilities. The bootstrapped-startup reported a revenue of ₹19.
paragraph3: 4 Cr in FY26, up about 50% YoY from around ₹13 Cr earned in FY25. As per Aminu’s website, it sources ingredients for its skincare products from over 40 countries, and features over 250 total ingredients across its product portfolio. It also claims to use only clean, skin friendly ingredients, having eliminated almost 3,000 such popular ingredients from its products. In the past, Nykaa has fully or partially acquired a number of BPC brands to place them under its house of brands.
paragraph4: This includes brands like Dot & Key and Earth Rhythm. Alongside approving the acquisition, Nykaa’s board also cleared the company’s financial performance for the first quarter of FY27. In the quarter, Nykaa reported an over 3X jump in its consolidated net profit for Q1 FY27 to ₹79.8 Cr from ₹24.
paragraph5: 8 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Meanwhile, its operating revenue jumped 29% YoY and 5% QoQ to ₹2,782 Cr.
