title: Legal AI startup Aavalynx raises £1.5M to cut the cost of corporate disputes
title_bn: Legal AI startup Aavalynx raises £1.5M to cut the cost of corporate disputes
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Legaltech Aavalynx has raised £1.5 million in pre-seed funding to help enterprises tackle the financial risk of legal disputes. Founded in 2023 and commercially live in 2024, Aavalynx has developed p...
paragraph1: Legaltech Aavalynx has raised £1.5 million in pre-seed funding to help enterprises tackle the financial risk of legal disputes. Founded in 2023 and commercially live in 2024, Aavalynx has developed proprietary AI tech that enables legal teams, law firms and litigation funders to structure, analyse, and interrogate dispute data at scale. It helps companies intervene earlier, make better-informed strategic decisions, improve litigation outcomes, and regain control over legal spend. I spoke to Hanna Roos, founder and CEO of Aavalynx, to learn more. The hidden cost of corporate litigation Today, about 30 per cent of total corporate external legal spend is on litigation, and 80 per cent of companies were involved in at least one lawsuit in 2025, with more than 46 per cent expecting an increase in lawsuits, according to a 2026 study survey of US corporate counsel. Despite the scale of this risk, organisations still lack the structured data and tools to systematically analyse dispute portfolios, identify emerging trends, or forecast likely outcomes with accuracy. As a result, they remain heavily dependent on external law firms for strategic decision-making. Yet classic law firm models are not equipped to provide a holistic risk assessment, for example, the impact on reputation and customer trust. Roos brings almost two decades of legal experience, having led complex, high-stakes international disputes in roles at Freshfields, Latham & Watkins, and Quinn Emanuel. Roos says the idea for Aavalynx emerged after years of seeing the same structural problems repeated across high-value disputes. “I loved the business of disputes. At university I was fascinated by Plato and Aristotle and their vision of how to live well, and by the idea that you could help deliver justice internationally through global disputes.” But once she started practising, she realised there were three fundamental problems. The first concerns law firms and the difference between the business of law, which is what law firms do, and law for business, which is what in-house legal teams need to deliver.
paragraph2: "Traditional law firm models are based on volume and hourly billing. Clients don't pass resolutions based on volume, but if your business model depends on volume, that's what happens. The average dispute involving states lasts 4.8 years. That's an average, and it's incredibly high.” Disputes often run for several years, if not decades, and can cost enterprise clients hundreds of millions per year. The total exposure of ongoing cases can greatly exceed a company’s annual revenue. In some cases, law firm profit margins can approach 80 per cent. Further, according to Roos, the larger the company's revenue, the larger its disputes portfolio. “To anonymise actual figures, you might have a business generating $50 billion in revenue with annual legal spending on disputes alone of around $200 million.” She further shared that if you compare the size of a company's disputes portfolio, particularly in sectors like defence, that portfolio is effectively a risk asset. “The total exposure can greatly exceed annual turnover, meaning the company is carrying a significant sub-optimal risk asset on its balance sheet.” The second problem is with in-house legal teams. She contends that when LLMs first emerged, her team started looking at the in-house space and realised many organisations didn't readily know where their data sat or how to harness it effectively. “That leads to a lack of transparency, slower decision-making and sub-optimal processes.
paragraph3: ” The third issue is the lawyers themselves. Roos contends that law is a sector built entirely around talent, but it doesn't always recognise that. “If you harness AI properly, combine it with good leadership and bring cognitive science into the way teams operate, suddenly you can deliver brilliant results without humans burning out. My tagline is "bringing joy back to lawyers."” Building AI to prevent disputes, not just manage them Currently, there's an abundance of legal AI tools from companies such as Harvey and Legora designed to improve lawyer productivity. Roos believes Aavalynx is solving a different problem. “Current AI tools by and large improve lawyer efficiency,” said Roos. “But efficiency is not good enough. Generic LLM models cannot address the unique complexities of a sector like dispute resolution. Good tools make disputes efficient, but great ones make them disappear. Even affirmative litigation (for a tech company pushing licence fees) should be as short and impactful as possible." Aavalynx gives companies the data and visibility to make better decisions earlier in the lifecycle of a dispute, where the financial impact is greatest. That shifts them from reactive firefighting to proactive decision-making. If clients can better understand their data, dispute length and cost won’t run wild.” Today, organisations have entire ecosystems involved in disputes, including external law firms, in-house teams, financial experts and local legal teams.
paragraph4: “It's not unusual to have twenty people working on a single matter,” Roos reveals. Avalynx aims to provide one central repository for information on a dispute. “I think of Aavalynx as the control panel of an aircraft. If you're the pilot, what information do you need in front of you to fly safely? We bring everyone onto that platform so they can make more strategic decisions and resolve disputes faster.” ​ Making the business case for legal AI When it comes to measuring the success of legal AI, Roos argues there are two distinct levels. “The first is straightforward: if you're the Head of Disputes or General Counsel, your role is to solve difficult business problems. The question is whether you're resolving disputes more effectively and what financial impact that creates. The second is demonstrating the overall value the legal function delivers to the business.” Roos believes this is particularly important for in-house legal teams, which are often viewed as a cost centre despite creating significant commercial value. “The best lawyers in private practice are seen as revenue generators. When those same brilliant lawyers move in-house, they suddenly become part of the back office and are viewed as a cost. But they're creating enormous value for the organisation.” Legal AI can help quantify that contribution through measurable outcomes. “If you can resolve disputes three years earlier than expected, reduce legal fees by $30 million, save another $40 million on quantum, or preserve a contract by avoiding reputational damage, you've demonstrated value not just on individual disputes but across the entire portfolio."
paragraph5: The data allows a team to identify patterns: "Perhaps procurement is responsible for a disproportionate number of disputes. You can work with that team, improve the underlying business process and prevent those disputes from arising in the future. Ultimately, it's about putting in-house legal teams in a position where they can articulate the value they create using data." Roos further says enterprise clients increasingly want AI investments to deliver measurable commercial outcomes. “Clients want to know: what savings have been generated for us? How has AI improved outcomes?” As a result, Aavalynx is developing a billing analytics capability. Clients will be able to understand how work is being delivered and where value is being created, rather than simply looking at hours billed. Legal AI needs evidence, not hallucinations Aavalynx was designed to minimise hallucinations by grounding its AI in evidence rather than relying on the model's general knowledge. Roos recalled her own experience, sharing: “I was working on a live dispute when a client called and said, ‘I’ve proved that the chair of this tribunal is corrupt. ChatGPT found two articles they co-authored with the opposing lawyer’s spouse.” The articles looked completely legitimate.

title: Google Drive finally fixes the most tedious part of reviewing videos
title_bn: Google Drive finally fixes the most tedious part of reviewing videos
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Your "skip to 2:14" messages are finally becoming a thing of the past.
paragraph1: Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityTL;DR Google Drive now lets you leave comments at exact moments in videos, making feedback much more precise. Timestamped comments work alongside regular comments, replies, @mentions, and other existing collaboration tools. The feature is enabled by default for Workspace and personal Google accounts, but timestamped comments can only be created on the web. Giving feedback on a video shouldn’t feel like solving a puzzle. Yet if you’ve ever reviewed a video stored in Google Drive, you’ve probably found yourself typing something like, “At 1:42, the text needs to be bigger,” or “Around 3:15, can you remove that transition?
paragraph2: ” It works, but it’s hardly the fastest or cleanest way to collaborate.Google is finally fixing that annoyance. The company is rolling out timestamped comments for videos in Google Drive on the web, making it much easier to leave feedback at the exact moment something happens in a video.For instance, you’re reviewing a YouTube video or a marketing video with your team. Rather than sending separate messages with timestamps or asking, “Which part are you talking about?
paragraph3: ”, editors can simply click the comment and jump straight to the relevant moment in the video.Google isn’t replacing regular comments, though. When leaving feedback, you’ll be able to choose between adding a timestamped comment tied to a specific point in the video or a standard comment that applies to the file as a whole. Existing collaboration tools, including replies, comment resolution, edits, and @mentions, continue to work alongside the new feature.There is one small limitation to keep in mind.
paragraph4: Timestamped comments can only be created from Google Drive on the web. If someone opens the same video from the Google Drive app on Android or iPhone, they’ll still see those comments, but they’ll appear as regular file comments instead of being linked to a precise moment in the video.The good news is that you won’t need to enable anything. Google says the feature is turned on by default and doesn’t require any administrator controls. It’s rolling out to Google Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and even personal Google accounts, so whether you’re editing videos for work, school, or your own YouTube channel, leaving precise feedback in Drive is about to get a whole lot easier.

title: AI-Native CRM Startup Superleap Bags ₹36 Cr Led By Peak XV’s Surge
title_bn: AI-Native CRM Startup Superleap Bags ₹36 Cr Led By Peak XV’s Surge
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Enterprise tech startup Superleap has raised ₹36 Cr (around $4.2 Mn) in its pre-Series A funding round led by Peak…
paragraph1: SUMMARYEnterprise tech startup Superleap has raised ₹36 Cr in a pre-Series A funding round led by Peak XV Partners' Surge The funding comes as enterprises increasingly adopt AI-native CRM platforms to replace legacy systems with AI-powered automation Superleap will use the fresh capital to expand its enterprise go-to-market efforts, strengthen its platform, and accelerate AI-native CRM adoption in India Enterprise tech startup Superleap has raised ₹36 Cr (around $4.2 Mn) in its pre-Series A funding round led by Peak XV Partners’ Surge. The Bengaluru-based startup said it will use the fresh capital to expand its enterprise go-to-market efforts, accelerate adoption of AI-native customer relationship management (CRM) platforms in India, and strengthen its product and platform capabilities. Founded in 2024 by former Unacademy executives Subham Kumar Boundia, Alok Maurya, and Saurabh Maheshwari, Superleap is building an AI-native CRM platform for enterprise revenue teams.
paragraph2: Positioning itself as an alternative to legacy CRM platforms, the startup claims it can reduce deployment timelines from months to weeks while enabling enterprises to migrate without disrupting business operations. Its platform comprises SuperOS, a unified data layer powering enterprise intelligence, and SuperAgents, an agentic layer that automates tasks across the revenue cycle. The platform also includes AI voice bots, conversational intelligence, Superleap AI, and MCP integrations with tools such as WhatsApp, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Claude, and ChatGPT. Its Superleap Deploy is designed to help enterprises migrate from legacy CRM systems through its forward-deployed engineering model.
paragraph3: The startup claims to have grown 10X over the past year and built a customer base spanning BFSI, SaaS, education, healthcare, travel and hospitality, and media. Its customers include Razorpay, Aakash Education, MediBuddy, HCL GUVI, Cars24, PagarBook, Plum, Qube Cinema, and Superhealth. Highlighting customer deployments, Superleap said Razorpay migrated more than 10 Mn records to its platform within 45 days without business disruption. It added that Aakash Education transitioned nearly 5,000 counsellors across 400 locations in under 60 days.
paragraph4: The funding comes amid growing enterprise demand for AI-native software that goes beyond traditional record-keeping to automate workflows and improve revenue generation. SaaS startups across CRM, sales automation, ERP, billing, and human resource management are increasingly pitching AI-first alternatives to legacy enterprise software. For instance, AI-powered SaaS startup Kris@Work raised $3 Mn in its seed round earlier this yea to offer an agentic AI-based, end-to-end platform for go-to-market (GTM) teams, including sales, marketing, revenue, and growth, to eliminate the need for multiple SaaS tools. The surge in enterprise AI also reflects a broader funding boom across India’s AI ecosystem.
paragraph5: According to Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, H1 2026’, Indian AI startups raised $676 Mn during the first six months of 2026, up 4X YoY.

title: Multi-day energy storage startup Ore Energy clinches $43M in new investment round
title_bn: Multi-day energy storage startup Ore Energy clinches $43M in new investment round
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Dutch energy storage startup Ore Energy has raised more than $40m, as it looks to commercialise its long-storage batteries.The $43m Series A funding round was led by two new investors, tech-investor P...
paragraph1: Dutch energy storage startup Ore Energy has raised more than $40m, as it looks to commercialise its long-storage batteries. The $43m Series A funding round was led by two new investors, tech-investor Plural and HV Capital, the European early-stage and growth VC firm. The round also included investment from Amsterdam VC Positron Ventures.
paragraph2: The funding brings the company’s total raised to $61m. Ore Energy’s tech is looking to solve a key bottleneck in the energy transition to renewables, which is storage. It says its iron-ore batteries can store electricity for up to 100 hours, unlike lithium-ion batteries, which typically deliver energy over a few hours.
paragraph3: Advocates of its tech say it will transform how we power industry, scale AI data centres and drive economic growth. Built using iron, water and air, Ore Energy say its batteries can be manufactured through a fully European supply chain, without relying on imported critical raw materials like lithium or cobalt. Ore Energy has signed what it says is the largest long-duration energy storage system deal in continental Europe, with Dutch energy supplier Budget Thuis.

paragraph1: Bulgaria-based Estel Technologies has raised €270,000 in pre-seed funding to expand its AI-native sales platform for the global tech talent industry. The round was led by Vitosha Ventures, with participation from Austrian angel investor Kerem Basak, founder and CEO of FB Consulting.
paragraph2: Founded by Bogdan Stavrev, Ivo Michorov and Yusuf Berki, Estel is developing an AI-powered workspace designed to help technology staffing firms identify, verify and prioritise sales opportunities. The platform combines demand verification, lead scoring and buyer matching in a single system, replacing the multiple disconnected tools typically used by recruiters and staffing sales teams.
paragraph3: The company is addressing inefficiencies in a global tech staffing market where recruiters often rely on outdated or duplicate job listings and fragmented workflows. Estel's proprietary Demand Confidence Score analyses market signals, verifies active hiring demand, ranks opportunities for individual users and automatically matches them with prospective buyers most likely to convert.
paragraph4: The new funding will be used to strengthen the platform's core technology, including its demand verification, scoring and matching algorithms, accelerate customer growth across key European markets, and support the company's progress towards a seed funding round and planned expansion into the US in 2027.

title: WhatsApp Tests Age Verification; Some Users Report Accounts Under Review
title_bn: WhatsApp Tests Age Verification; Some Users Report Accounts Under Review
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Meta-owned WhatsApp is testing privacy-protective ways to verify users’ age ahead of the rollout of India’s Digital Personal Data Protection…
paragraph1: SUMMARYWhatsApp is testing privacy-protective age verification methods, including optional date-of-birth prompts for select users, to prepare for compliance with India's DPDP Act before it comes into force in May 2027 The rollout signals that digital platforms are proactively preparing for the DPDP regime, which is expected to reshape how user data is collected and processed in India Separately, WhatsApp acknowledged that some users' accounts were mistakenly placed under review as part of its efforts to curb platform abuse and said it is working to restore affected accounts quickly Meta-owned WhatsApp is testing privacy-protective ways to verify users’ age ahead of the rollout of India’s Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, which is set to come into force in May next year. “To comply with upcoming laws in India like the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, we are testing privacy-protective ways for people to confirm their age,” a WhatsApp spokesperson said. Earlier this week, several social media users claimed they received a prompt on WhatsApp asking them to add their date of birth to their profile to comply with upcoming Indian regulations. WhatsApp clarified that only a limited set of users received the prompt as part of an ongoing test and that providing the information remains optional. The company added that it will process the information in line with its privacy commitments and will not make it visible to other users. The development was first reported by technology newsletter ‘TheTechTrace’.
paragraph2: Notably, the DPDP Act does not mandate users to verify their age or require minors to disclose it. Instead, the law requires platforms to obtain verifiable parental or guardian consent before processing the personal data of children and exercise due diligence to establish the age of users and the authority of those providing consent. Platforms can fulfil these obligations using reliable age or identity information already available with them or through information voluntarily provided via authorised entities. Separately, several WhatsApp users reported yesterday that their accounts were placed under review without prior notice. Affected users received a notification stating, “Account in review. Date requested: 3 Aug 2026.
paragraph3: Your account activity and device info is being checked to make sure it follows our terms of service. We will notify you of the result typically within 24 hours.” Several users claimed the temporary suspension disrupted their work. While WhatsApp acknowledged the issue, it did not specify what triggered the reviews, whether they were linked to a particular policy violation, or if users in specific regions were affected. “We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting,” PTI quoted a WhatsApp spokesperson as saying.
paragraph4: Meta Under The Scanner In India Meta has come under increased regulatory scrutiny in India over its handling of content moderation during recent student protests in the national capital. Last week, Meta India vice president and head Arun Srinivas was named in an FIR filed in Hyderabad over allegedly objectionable content circulated on the company’s platforms. The FIR also named operators of multiple Facebook and Instagram accounts accused of sharing morphed content targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The case followed another controversy in which Facebook temporarily removed a video posted by PM Modi. Meta later restored the post, attributing the takedown to an error in its AI-powered content moderation system. According to PTI, Meta told the IT ministry that such posts will now undergo additional oversight and require approval from at least two senior executives before any moderation decision is taken.
paragraph5: The company also expressed regret over the incident and outlined corrective measures. Separately, the IT ministry earlier this month asked WhatsApp to pause the rollout of its username feature in India over concerns that usernames resembling those of individuals, financial institutions or government agencies could enable impersonation, phishing and online fraud.

title: Apple Restores Telegram On App Store After Brief CSAM-Related Takedown
title_bn: Apple Restores Telegram On App Store After Brief CSAM-Related Takedown
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple briefly removed Telegram from its App Store globally yesterday after an App Store review identified content that violated its…
paragraph1: SUMMARYApple briefly removed Telegram from the App Store after finding content related to child sexual abuse material but restored it after Telegram the content was removed The incident renews concerns over Telegram's content moderation practices as the messaging platform faces mounting regulatory scrutiny across countries, including India Telegram was unavailable for new downloads for a short time before Apple restored it. Telegram appeared to make light of the incident, saying, “Reports of my demise are greatly exaggerated” Apple briefly removed Telegram from its App Store globally yesterday after an App Store review identified content that violated its policies on child sexual abuse material (CSAM). The iPhone maker later restored the messaging app after the said content was removed. The iPhone maker said Telegram was reinstated after “the developer promptly removed the content and banned the user who posted it”. For a brief period, Telegram’s App Store listing displayed a message stating, “The page you’re looking for can’t be found,” making the app unavailable for new downloads.
paragraph2: Existing users, however, continued to access the service, while Telegram remained available on the Google Play Store and the Mac App Store. Telegram later confirmed that the app returned to Apple’s marketplace, saying, “Telegram has been restored on the App Store and should soon be available again for all users,” without elaborating on the incident. According to Bloomberg, Apple removed the app after an App Store review identified content that breached its strict rules on CSAM. In response to the allegations, Telegram said in a statement, “Apple reported one user sharing CSAM, who was immediately banned. Telegram has removed more than 337,900 groups and channels related to CSAM in 2026.
paragraph3: ” After the restoration, Telegram appeared to make light of the incident, posting on X: “Reports of my demise are greatly exaggerated.” The latest episode echoes a similar incident in 2018, when Apple removed both Telegram and its alternative client app Telegram X from the App Store after determining that users could access inappropriate content, including CSAM, through the platforms. Telegram later introduced additional safeguards, following which both apps were reinstated. Telegram Faces Growing Regulatory Heat In India The latest development comes amid mounting regulatory scrutiny of Telegram in India over concerns ranging from piracy and cybercrime to drug trafficking and examination paper leaks. Most recently, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting issued a notice to Telegram over the alleged circulation of pirated films and OTT content on the platform.
paragraph4: The ministry directed the messaging app to submit an action taken report within 15 days and explain its grievance redressal mechanism for producers, OTT platforms and law enforcement agencies. The platform has also come under the scanner over its username-based identity feature. Earlier, the Centre sought an explanation from Telegram on why the functionality should continue to be offered, raising concerns over its potential misuse. Similar queries were also sent to Signal regarding safeguards on its platform. Separately, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), in its 2025 annual report, identified Telegram as a major platform for advertising illegal narcotics.
paragraph5: The agency said the app’s public channels and ease of access make it an attractive medium for traffickers to promote drugs. Responding to these concerns, Telegram said criminal activity exists across online platforms but maintained that it actively combats misuse through “industry-leading moderation” that removes millions of harmful posts every day. Telegram has also been embroiled in the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak controversy. During proceedings before the Delhi High Court, the Centre described the platform as the “new dark web”, arguing that its cloud-based architecture, public channels, bots, large groups and username-based identities enable activities such as cyber fraud, financial scams, drug trafficking, child exploitation, piracy and terrorism. As part of its submissions, the government also pointed to a Telegram channel named “NEET Mafia”, which allegedly circulated content related to the paper leak, including advance booking arrangements, and payment mechanisms.

title: The Next Frontier For Faith Commerce
title_bn: The Next Frontier For Faith Commerce
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Running out of pooja samagri just before an aarti is no longer the household crisis it once was. The missing…
paragraph1: SUMMARYThanks to the rising bandwagon of 900+ new-age D2C brands, the Indian spiritual or faith commerce ecosystem has come a long way over the past decade For decades, VCs found it difficult to invest in faith commerce. This is because the market was largely cash-based, fragmented, offline and culturally sensitive India’s spiritual economy is estimated at approximately $60-70 Bn, while funding into spiritual tech companies has accelerated materially over the past few years Running out of pooja samagri just before an aarti is no longer the household crisis it once was. The missing camphor, flowers or diya can now arrive at your doorstep within minutes. A gemstone recommended during an online astrology consultation can be bought before the call is over. Even prasad and blessed products can travel from a temple to a devotee living in another city or country without any hassle. Thanks to the rising bandwagon of 900+ new-age D2C brands, such as Phool, Astroyogi, Japam, Sri Mandir and Vama, among others, the Indian spiritual or faith commerce ecosystem has come a long way over the past decade. For decades, VCs found it difficult to invest in faith commerce. This is because the market was largely cash-based, fragmented, offline and culturally sensitive. But times have changed. India’s faith ecommerce market has been successful in grabbing eyeballs. According to experts, India’s spiritual economy is estimated at approximately $60-70 Bn, while funding into spiritual tech companies has accelerated materially over the past few years. Abishek Balendran, partner, SilverX Fund & Silverneedle Ventures believes the interesting bit isn’t that faith suddenly became a venture category. It’s that India’s digital infrastructure has finally made faith-centric D2C commerce measurable, repeatable and scalable.
paragraph2: Three significant factors have powered this shift: Digital Infrastructure: UPI and smartphones made faith services easier to access and enabled seamless, low-value digital transactions. Regional Language Internet: Non-English internet adoption in India brought the category’s core consumers online, significantly expanding the addressable market. Pandemic-Driven Behaviour: Covid-19 accelerated digital adoption across age groups, encouraging founders to build trusted, convenient and personalised faith experiences online. “The other major unlock has been the diaspora opportunity. For an Indian living in New York or Dubai, access is a problem. Technology solves that. When you see platforms deriving a meaningful share of revenue from international users who are willing to pay a premium to stay connected to their roots, it fundamentally changes the total addressable market,” said Padamaja Ruparel, cofounder, Indian Angel Network. But as the sector matures, several questions emerge. Can faith commerce produce enduring, venture-scale businesses? And what challenges must founders overcome to unlock the market’s full potential? No Longer A Niche Bet India’s D2C spiritual tech market is rapidly evolving from a niche digital experiment into a meaningful consumer internet category. While astrology took more than a decade to establish itself online, temple-led commerce began gaining traction only after the pandemic. But that gap is now narrowing.
paragraph3: Vama offers an early glimpse of this shift. According to cofounder Manu Jain, temple-led products emerged as a breakout vertical for the company, helping it grow its revenue 3X by June 2026 compared with the previous financial year. The demand is also spreading across categories. Astroyogi serves more than 40 Mn users across consultations, tarot, numerology and retail, while its retail business, Yogii, launched two years ago, is growing by around 50% QoQ. “The opportunity is not to create a new market, but to make a large, fragmented market more accessible, convenient and organised,” said Astroyogi’s cofounder Meena Kapoor. Meanwhile, AstroTalk showed just how large that opportunity could become. Its spiritual-products division crossed ₹140 Cr in revenue in its first year and recently crossed a daily GMV run rate of around ₹1 Cr in August 2025. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU The company reported revenues of ₹1,182 Cr in FY25 and a ₹250 Cr net profit. It is targeting a ₹2,000 Cr run rate ahead of a planned IPO in late 2026 or early 2027. If successful, it would become India’s first listed consumer astrology company. Naturally, investor interest has followed. For D2C faith commerce, the biggest challenge is convincing consumers that what they see online is genuine. This is particularly difficult in categories such as gemstones, where buyers may be unable to verify authenticity or identify treatments.
paragraph4: The proliferation of fake websites and dropshippers makes that trust deficit harder to address. For investors, the concern is when a product or service cannot be independently verified. Vama counters this by sending temple certificates with spiritual products and sharing videos of items being energised at the temple. It also reinforces its status as an authorised temple partner throughout the customer journey. According to Vama’s Jain, the hardest operational challenge, apart from trust, is managing logistics and execution during festivals such as Diwali, when demand can spike sharply. Companies should be able to forecast inventory, distribute stock across fulfilment centres and coordinate execution seamlessly. Jain also believes technology should complement, not replace, the offline faith experience. Devotees still want a connection with the temple, and digital platforms work best when they strengthen that relationship. Companies that can preserve this authenticity while managing trust, logistics and seasonal demand will be better positioned to build loyal customers in an increasingly competitive market. Nevertheless, not all are blessed in the faith economy. In May 2026, spiritual tech startup DevDham (formerly DevDarshan) shut down roughly two years after its major seed funding round. The startup failed due to monetisation challenges, scaling pressures and failed acquisition talks. The Next Big Moat Going forward, IAN’s Ruparel expects the product layer to remain fragmented because anyone can launch devotional merchandise.
paragraph5: Consultation businesses will continue to grow because they have exceptionally strong retention. But the real value will accrue to companies that own the customer relationship. Access is where the analysts see the most durable moat. If a platform becomes the default gateway for discovering temples, booking pilgrimages, making donations, accessing content and purchasing associated products, it benefits from powerful network effects. The ecosystem expects darshan and access to consolidate naturally, as a temple is unlikely to grant exclusive digital rights to multiple platforms. This makes supply relationships defensible and creates a high-frequency, relatively low-CAC entry point. “Access by itself is not where the biggest margins sit, but it becomes the moat. Astrology has very low barriers to entry, so it tends to fragment and become price-competitive. Ecommerce, meanwhile, has super-high gross margins, monetises the believer’s full wallet and scales,” said Silverneedle’s Balendran. Meanwhile, Ujwal Sutaria, founder and managing partner at TDV Partners believes access has the best economics because it has scarce supply, inelastic demand, high average order value and no cost of goods sold (COGS) drag. Whoever locks up the temple towns that matter will be hard to dislodge. Over the next five years, the winners will look less like ecommerce companies and more like consumer platforms with multiple monetisation engines. They can win one layer of the stack, use ownership of access to build the customer relationship and then monetise that relationship through commerce over time.

Vama counters this by sending temple certificates with spiritual products and sharing videos of items being energised at the temple. It also reinforces its status as an authorised temple partner throughout the customer journey. According to Vama’s Jain, the hardest operational challenge, apart from trust, is managing logistics and execution during festivals such as Diwali, when demand can spike sharply. Companies should be able to forecast inventory, distribute stock across fulfilment centres and coordinate execution seamlessly. Jain also believes technology should complement, not replace, the offline faith experience. Devotees still want a connection with the temple, and digital platforms work best when they strengthen that relationship. Companies that can preserve this authenticity while managing trust, logistics and seasonal demand will be better positioned to build loyal customers in an increasingly competitive market. Nevertheless, not all are blessed in the faith economy. In May 2026, spiritual tech startup DevDham (formerly DevDarshan) shut down roughly two years after its major seed funding round. The startup failed due to monetisation challenges, scaling pressures and failed acquisition talks. The Next Big Moat Going forward, IAN’s Ruparel expects the product layer to remain fragmented because anyone can launch devotional merchandise.
bangla_paragraph5: Consultation businesses will continue to grow because they have exceptionally strong retention. But the real value will accrue to companies that own the customer relationship. Access is where the analysts see the most durable moat. If a platform becomes the default gateway for discovering temples, booking pilgrimages, making donations, accessing content and purchasing associated products, it benefits from powerful network effects. The ecosystem expects darshan and access to consolidate naturally, as a temple is unlikely to grant exclusive digital rights to multiple platforms. This makes supply relationships defensible and creates a high-frequency, relatively low-CAC entry point. “Access by itself is not where the biggest margins sit, but it becomes the moat. Astrology has very low barriers to entry, so it tends to fragment and become price-competitive. Ecommerce, meanwhile, has super-high gross margins, monetises the believer’s full wallet and scales,” said Silverneedle’s Balendran. Meanwhile, Ujwal Sutaria, founder and managing partner at TDV Partners believes access has the best economics because it has scarce supply, inelastic demand, high average order value and no cost of goods sold (COGS) drag. Whoever locks up the temple towns that matter will be hard to dislodge. Over the next five years, the winners will look less like ecommerce companies and more like consumer platforms with multiple monetisation engines. They can win one layer of the stack, use ownership of access to build the customer relationship and then monetise that relationship through commerce over time.

title: Apple is finally closing a significant ecosystem gap with Android on Windows
title_bn: Apple is finally closing a significant ecosystem gap with Android on Windows
author: TechPulse
excerpt: One of Apple's biggest ecosystem perks is finally coming to Windows.
paragraph1: Tushar Mehta / Android AuthorityTL;DR Apple is finally working on iPhone-to-Windows clipboard syncing after a Microsoft interoperability request in the EU. The feature will let users copy and paste between an iPhone and a Windows PC, similar to Apple’s Universal Clipboard. Android users have had this functionality for years through Microsoft’s Phone Link and SwiftKey. Apple is finally working on a feature that Android users have enjoyed for years.
paragraph2: As part of the European Union’s interoperability requirements, Apple has confirmed (via MacRumors) that it’s developing a way for users to seamlessly copy and paste content between an iPhone and a paired Windows PC.The move comes after Microsoft requested the feature, saying that Windows users should have the same cross-device clipboard functionality that Apple already offers between Macs, iPhones, and iPads through its Universal Clipboard.AppleIf this sounds familiar, it’s because Android users have long had a similar functionality through Microsoft’s Phone Link app and the SwiftKey Keyboard. Both of these apps support clipboard syncing with Android devices, and have done so for years.
paragraph3: Apple’s implementation will work a little differently under the hood, though.According to Apple’s interoperability documentation, developers will be able to build an extension that shares clipboard (pasteboard) content with paired accessories, including Windows PCs. Whenever a user copies something on their iPhone, iOS will notify the extension, which can then securely transfer the clipboard contents to the paired device using Apple’s Accessory Transport Extension framework.AppleMicrosoft had requested persistent clipboard access from Apple, and the Cupertino company initially said it needed to evaluate whether the feature was technically feasible and if it could preserve iOS security and integrity.
paragraph4: Later on, Apple decided to proceed with the solution, describing the project as a “significant engineering effort” that will not wrap up until fall 2027.That said, since the solution is currently part of Apple’s EU interoperability process, it could be limited to users in the European Union. Microsoft will also need to use Apple’s AccessorySetupKit framework to obtain user permission for every paired Windows PC before clipboard syncing can begin.FollowThank you for being part of our community.

title: Telegram app back on Apple's App Store after removal over child sexual abuse material: Report
title_bn: Telegram app back on Apple's App Store after removal over child sexual abuse material: Report
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Telegram announced its messaging app is back on the App Store after being removed for violating guidelines regarding child sexual abuse material.
paragraph1: Telegram announced its messaging app is back on the App Store after being removed for violating guidelines regarding child sexual abuse material.Telegram access restricted in India after NTA's recommendation. (Representative image)(Pexels)Telegram said on Monday that its app was back on the App Store, as per a Reuters report. The popular messaging app had earlier disappeared from Apple's App Store without any reason being given by either Apple or Telegram."Telegram has been restored on the App Store and should soon be available again for all users," the company said.After the Telegram app had disappeared, the App Store page read, "The page you're looking for can't be found."As per Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple had briefly removed the Telegram app from the App Store after its review found the app in violation of the App Store's guidelines on child sexual abuse material.
paragraph2: The app was reportedly later reinstated after Telegram removed the sexual content and banned the user who had posted it.Notably, Telegram continued to be available on the Google Play Store and via the Mac App Store. Moreover, existing Telegram users continued to be able to access the app without reporting any loss of data. The App Store ban also does not appear to have affected users in India so far.Telegram's official handle on X (formerly Twitter) joked about the brief removal of the app in a new post, writing, "Reports of my demise are greatly exaggerated 🍎"Apple and Telegram's history:Notably, this is not the first time that Apple has taken down the Telegram app from the App Store. The company had also briefly removed the popular messaging app from its App Store over the presence of child sexual abuse material.Similar to the current incident, the Telegram app was restored to the App Store after the illegal content was taken down and the user who had posted it was banned from the platform.
paragraph3: Telegram's regulatory hurdles:Telegram has also faced regulatory hurdles in recent years. Telegram CEO Pavel Durov was arrested in France in 2024 over the app's alleged failure to stop the spread of child sexual abuse material.Durov faced preliminary charges related to a lack of app moderation, drug trafficking and facilitating illicit transactions. However, the Telegram CEO was later released on bail and allowed to leave France.Meanwhile, a few days back, Russia charged the Telegram founder with offences related to facilitating terrorist activity and accused the platform of being run by Ukrainian intelligence services to recruit Russians for attacks inside the country.Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) also placed Durov on an international wanted list.About the AuthorAman GuptaAman Gupta is a Digital Content Producer at LiveMint with over 3.
paragraph4:

His reporting is grounded in first-hand testing, independent analysis, and a focus on how technology impacts everyday users. He holds a PG Diploma in Radio and Television Journalism from the Indian Institute of Mass Communication, Delhi (Class of 2022).

title: Telegram’s Apple App Store mystery continues, but it’s still available on Android
title_bn: Telegram’s Apple App Store mystery continues, but it’s still available on Android
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Telegram says its app is once again available on Apple's App Store, but a complete restoration appears to be pending.
paragraph1: Stephen Headrick / Android AuthorityTL;DR Telegram disappeared from Apple’s App Store in multiple countries on Monday for unknown reasons. The company says the app has been restored, but it still isn’t showing up on the App Store. Meanwhile, the messaging app remains available on the Google Play Store, so Android users are unaffected. Telegram disappeared from Apple’s App Store on Monday in what appears to have been a worldwide issue.
paragraph2: While Telegram now says the app has been restored, its return doesn’t seem to be complete just yet.Earlier on Monday, users across multiple countries noticed that searching for Telegram on the App Store no longer returned the app. Existing users with Telegram already installed on their iPhones and iPads could continue using it, but new downloads were unavailable.Interestingly, the app continued to appear on the Mac App Store and never disappeared from the Google Play Store.
paragraph3: Telegram acknowledged the issue and gave the following statement to Reuters, without explaining why the app disappeared in the first place: Telegram has been restored on the App Store and should soon be available again for all users. Despite Telegram’s statement, the rollout of the restoration appears to be ongoing or incomplete. At the time of writing this article, we still can’t find the Telegram app on Apple’s App Store. Visiting the direct App Store link results in an error page instead of the app listing, suggesting that the restoration is still pending across several regions.
paragraph4: The company also remained unusually quiet on social media about the App Store issue for hours. One of its most recent posts on X joked: “crazy that we’re gonna get GTA 6 before the full Epstein files.”TelegramThis was followed by another post just minutes before this article went live, saying, “reports of my demise are greatly exaggerated.”TelegramFor now, the disruption appears to be limited to Apple’s App Store.
paragraph5: Telegram remains available on Google Play, so Android users can still download and install the app without issue.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: Ather’s Stellar Q1, Klassroom IPO Day 2 & More
title_bn: Ather’s Stellar Q1, Klassroom IPO Day 2 & More
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Ather Turns A Corner Amid concerns of sliding EV two wheeler sales in India, Ather managed to sharply shrink its…
paragraph1: Ather Turns A Corner Amid concerns of sliding EV two wheeler sales in India, Ather managed to sharply shrink its losses in Q1 FY27, and more importantly, turn EBITDA positive. Bolstered by its fresh ₹2,500 Cr rights issue and fundraise, Ather is now preparing to scale its expansion plans and inch closer to real profitability. Here is a quick look at Ather’s Q1 FY27 numbers: Net loss narrowed 71% YoY to ₹51.1 Cr Operating revenue zoomed 89% YoY to ₹1,216.9 Cr Total expenses soared 54% YoY to ₹1,310.7 Cr EBITDA profit stood at ₹9 Cr versus an EBITDA loss of ₹106 Cr loss a year ago Volume Surges: The EBITDA turnaround was driven by strong volumes. The EV maker delivered 83,173 electric scooters in Q1, an 81% YoY jump, as customer demand continued to outstrip production capacity. On top of this, rising high-margin non-vehicle revenue from software subscriptions, charging, accessories and after-sales services contributed 14% of operating revenue. Margin Discipline: Despite commodity cost spikes, Ather expanded its adjusted gross margin by 82% YoY to ₹282 Cr in Q1. The EV maker managed to offset inflationary pressures through calibrated price hikes, supplier negotiations and an improved product mix. These measures unlocked strong operating leverage, helping Ather absorb fixed overheads. Ather’s Next Stop: To meet demand, Ather is now accelerating its manufacturing expansion. Its new unit in Maharashtra is on track to start production in Q3 FY27 and will add 5 Lakh units of annual capacity. Once fully operational, total capacity will reach 14.2 Lakh per year. In addition, the company plans to roll out a new scooter later this month to widen market share and sharpen manufacturing efficiency.
paragraph2: As the EV maker prepares to pour the recently raised funds to scale its ambitions, here is how Ather fared on the financial front in Q1… From The Editor’s Desk 🔔 Klassroom IPO Day 2 The edtech startup’s BSE SME IPO was subscribed 98% on the second day of bidding, receiving bids for 17.22 Lakh shares as against 17.58 Lakh shares on offer. Retail investors led from the front, oversubscribing their quota by 1.32X. Qualified institutional buyers and non-institutional investors also picked up pace and subscribed their portions 68% and 67%, respectively. Klassroom’s public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares up to 19.89 Lakh shares and an OFS of up to 4.66 Lakh shares. At the upper end of its price band of ₹151-159, Klassroom is looking to raise ₹39 Cr via the IPO at a valuation of ₹146 Cr. 💳 UPI MDR On The Anvil? The Centre has proposed new amendments to Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The draft rules replace the blanket prohibition on MDR and exempt only certain payment modes, notified by the government, from the charges. The proposed rules are expected to be tabled in the Parliament tomorrow. Industry players have welcomed the development, with many hinting that the proposed rules could move the pricing decision of the MDR directly under RBI control. This follows Inc42 reporting that the Centre was weighing a targeted reintroduction of MDR.
paragraph3: Under the proposal, businesses with an annual turnover of ₹1 Cr to ₹1.5 Cr or more would attract an MDR of 0.05% to 0.07% on UPI transactions above ₹2,000. 💰 Matel Motion Bags ₹130 Cr The EV components maker has raised around $13.6 Mn in its Series B round led by UC Impower to scale its manufacturing capacity, advance R&D, accelerate product development, ramp up hiring and broader international footprint. Founded in 2017, Matel designs and manufactures synchronous machines and motor controllers for e-mobility, industrial applications and agricultural pumps. It last raised $4 Mn in its Series A round in 2024. The homegrown EV component manufacturing ecosystem is witnessing a major boom, driven by government incentives, supply chain localisation efforts and growing consumer demand for green vehicles. 📈 Shiprocket Gears Up For IPO The ecommerce enablement unicorn plans to launch its IPO within the next two weeks at a valuation of ₹7,000 Cr. Having already received SEBI nod, Shiprocket now plans to file its updated IPO papers with SEBI in the coming days. Meanwhile, LEAP India has also filed its RHP with the markets regulator for a ₹2,480 Cr IPO. The logistics-focused SaaS platform has set a price band of ₹151-₹159 for its issue, which will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth ₹480 Cr and OFS of up to ₹2,000 Cr. Joining the IPO bandwagon, battery swapping startup Battery Smart is all set to file its DRHP with SEBI by October. The platform has raised more than $200 Mn to date, and operates a network of more than 1,500 swapping stations across 75+ cities. 🤝 Imarticus Acquires BELLS In its first international acquisition, the IPO-bound edtech startup has acquired the Singapore-based upskilling for ₹800 Cr.
paragraph4: The combined entity will have more than 1,100 employees and will operate across over 25 offices. As part of the deal, Imarticus plans to launch a new BELLS school to offer AI-related courses to help expand its presence in the Southeast Asian market. This is the homegrown startup’s second acquisition in less than a year, after MyCaptain. The deal comes as Imarticus is looking to list on the bourses, eyeing a ₹1,000 Cr IPO. Founded in 2012, the startup offers professional education, executive education and corporate training programmes across finance, technology and business. ✈️ MakeMyTrip’s Q1 Show The travel tech major’s consolidated net profit plunged 65% YoY to $9.1 Mn in Q1 FY27 despite the Nasdaq-listed company’s revenue growing 6% YoY to $285.6 Mn. The OTA attributed its subdued performance to the depreciation of the Indian Rupee against the US dollar and dampened international demand due to the ongoing West Asia conflict. However, strong seasonal demand partially offset these pressures. On the operational front, MakeMyTrip’s gross bookings rose 19.9% YoY in constant currency to $2.85 Bn, led by growth across air ticketing, hotels and packages, and bus ticketing. Inc42 Markets RECOMMENDED FOR yOU Inc42 Startup Spotlight Can FireAI Build An AI-Driven Decision Layer For Brands? For enterprises, the challenge has never been the lack of data. But turning this data into decisions is still slow, siloed and analyst-dependent.
paragraph5: FireAI wants to fix this by connecting fragmented systems and suggesting what to do next, all through simple AI queries. The Insight Layer: Founded in 2025, FireAI’s platform helps unify multiple data sources, traces performance dips through a causal chain and turns days of manual investigation into a structured analysis within minutes. This insight-led approach has helped the startup land 200+ clients like Bata, IRCTC and Plum. Under The Hood: FireAI sits on top of existing ERPs, CRMs, accounting tools, databases and marketing platforms, connecting 700+ sources without moving raw data out of customer infrastructure. It uses a multi-agent layer to map business context, relationships and formulas before generating SQL queries via a fine-tuned Llama 3.3 model. This orchestration, not the LLM itself, is the startup’s core moat. Breaking The Silo: FireAI charges an upfront integration fee plus subscription pricing, avoiding token-based billing. title: WhatsApp outage leaves thousands of users unable to share media; 'I thought my WiFi was trash'
title_bn: WhatsApp outage leaves thousands of users unable to share media; 'I thought my WiFi was trash'
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Thousands of WhatsApp users reported issues on Monday, unable to send media or create stories.
paragraph1: Thousands of WhatsApp users reported issues on Monday, unable to send media or create stories. A message can be pinned on WhatsApp for a maximum of 30 daysThousands of WhatsApp users on Monday complained about problems with the messaging platform, reporting that they were unable to send pictures, videos or create a Status update. According to the outage-tracking website Downdetector, the issue appears to have affected users across various parts of the world, including India, the US, Mexico and the UK."Whenever I try to send an image on WhatsApp, I get as far as the image appearing in the chat with a spinning wheel, then it just says 'retry'. I can still receive images and I can still send images in other apps. How can I fix this for WhatsApp?" wrote one user on Reddit."Oh how reassuring it was to Google 'why can't I send photos on WhatsApp' and be met with a thread made within the hour.
paragraph2: Don't make a girl look at settings after a long day," wrote another user."This is happening with recent photos/screenshots only. Even photos from the morning are sending easily," added another user."I uninstalled my #WhatsApp and accidentally deleted all my WhatsApp files (most importantly my stickers) just to realize it was a worldwide issue that has been going on 🥲🥲🥲🥲," wrote a user on X."And here I was thinking I had no data and that my WiFi was trash and nooo turns out WhatsApp crashed 💀🤦‍♀️," another user wrote.The issue, however, seems to have been resolved since then, with reports on Downdetector seeing a steady decline across various countries. However, an official statement from Meta or WhatsApp is still awaited on the matter.WhatsApp puts user accounts under review for 24 hoursIn related news, WhatsApp also placed many users' accounts under review for 24 hours, restricting access to all app features.
paragraph3: As per a PTI report, the issue surfaced around 8 pm IST, when users began reporting that their accounts had been placed under review.Affected users were reportedly shown a message on the app stating: "Account in review. Date requested: 3 Aug 2026. Your account activity and device info is being checked to make sure it follows our Terms of Service. We will notify you of the result, typically within 24 hours."The notification also included links to guidance on responsible use of WhatsApp and information about stolen phones and compromised accounts.Responding to the issue, a WhatsApp spokesperson told PTI that the company continuously works to prevent misuse of its platform but acknowledged that mistakes can occur."We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe.
paragraph4:
Sometimes we get this wrong, and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting," the spokesperson said.About the AuthorAman GuptaAman Gupta is a Digital Content Producer at LiveMint with over 3.5 years of experience covering the technology landscape. He specializes in artificial intelligence and consumer technology, reporting on everything from the ethical debates around AI models to shifts in the smartphone market.
His reporting is grounded in first-hand testing, independent analysis, and a focus on how technology impacts everyday users. He holds a PG Diploma in Radio and Television Journalism from the Indian Institute of Mass Communication, Delhi (Class of 2022).
Outside the newsroom, he spends his time reading biographies, hunting for the perfect coffee beans, or planning his next trip.

title: Ex-Delhivery, Cleartrip Execs Launch Profound To Bring AI-Powered Professional Support For Individuals
title_bn: Ex-Delhivery, Cleartrip Execs Launch Profound To Bring AI-Powered Professional Support For Individuals
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Ex-Delhivery tech head Prashant Parashar and ex-Cleartrip chief business and growth officer Anuj Rathi have joined hands to launch an…
paragraph1: SUMMARYProfound is building AI representatives for professionals akin to the managers employed by actors and athletes The newly launched venture has raised $1.5 Mn in seed funding from Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital, as well as several high-profile angel investors Its consumer business focuses on solving representation and connection. It also has a B2B vertical to help startups with recruitment Ex-Delhivery tech head Prashant Parashar and ex-Cleartrip chief business and growth officer Anuj Rathi have joined hands to launch an AI-native startup Profound. The startup is building an AI-powered assistant or “representative” that can support individuals in their professional lives. Profound claims that it can create AI representatives for professionals across fields, similar to the managers employed by athletes, actors and musicians. After a 30-minute voice conversation with the AI agent, its system learns the professional context of the user, including their expertise, experience, working style, career ambitions, among others.
paragraph2: Coming out of stealth, Profound has raised a $1.5 Mn seed funding round led by Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital. Several angel investors including Swiggy CEO Sriharsha Majety, Swiggy cofounder Nandan Reddy, Razorpay CEO Harshil Mathur, CRED founder and WhatsApp global head Kunal Shah, OfBusiness cofounder Bhuvan Gupta, and Zomato cofounder Pankaj Chaddah also backed the startup. Parashar, the startup’s CTO, has headed tech functions at startups like Delhivery, Snapdeal and Ola before he started up at Profound. On the other hand, Rathi led product and marketing at Jupiter and had a seven-year-long at Swiggy, scaling various initiatives like Instamart, Swiggy Labs, and Genie. The two have teamed up to launch a new venture at the intersection of recruitment, social media, and AI.
paragraph3: From a technical standpoint, Profound’s tech stack is divided into four layers – understanding, representation, connection, and amplification. The understanding layer combines voice AI, multimodal user interfaces, and a mix of large, small, and voice-specific models, including ElevenLabs’ models, OpenAI’s Sol, Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet, and Kimi AI. Then, the representation layer synthesises conversation data into authentic articulations of the user’s professional life based on the context. The platform then operates a proprietary matchmaking engine to proactively assist with networking. Finally, the amplification layer assists the user with building their personal brand and creating content that fits their identity. For consumers, the service aims to understand and articulate the user’s professional identity for use cases like resumes, job matching, among others.
paragraph4: It also has a social aspect to facilitate networking. Profound is also building a B2B side to help solve for startup hiring, Rathi told Inc42. The platform can help search for potential candidates, evaluate how well they fit in a role and identify points to be verified or examined further in their profile. While the consumer business will be subscription-based, the B2B vertical will charge companies a percentage based on the annual CTC of the positions to be recruited. “We are starting with a few specific domains tailored for AI-first professionals. On the tech side, we are focusing on engineering, product, and design (EPD) while on the non-tech side, we are catering to professionals in marketing, sales, and analytics roles,” said Rathi.
paragraph5: The startup claims to have already conducted 1,000+ calls as it aims to nail down its product-market fit. It has already made its product available to the public for users to have an introductory call with the AI agent, and will be rolling out features on an early-access basis in the next few months. It aims to achieve one million users who are actively engaging with their AI representatives within the next one year, per Rathi.

title: Agentic AI Startup Kily Raises ₹30 Cr To Accelerate Platform Deployment
title_bn: Agentic AI Startup Kily Raises ₹30 Cr To Accelerate Platform Deployment
author: TechPulse
excerpt: AI startup Kily has raised a ₹30 Cr ($3.2 Mn) in a funding round led by early stage VC firm…
paragraph1: SUMMARYKily has raised a ₹30 funding round led by Sorin Investments, with participation from Razorpay and Wyser Capital This comes amid a wave of capital backing startups aiming to help enterprises automate their workflows through the use of agentic AI Kily’s autonomous AI agents help consumer brands make decisions to drive growth on e-commerce marketplaces based on real-time data from the platform AI startup Kily has raised a ₹30 Cr ($3.2 Mn) in a funding round led by early stage VC firm Sorin Investments. Other investors that partook in the round included IPO-bound fintech major Razorpay and VC firm Wyser Capital. Kily will use the fresh capital to strengthen its product capabilities and go-to-market initiatives, as well as accelerate platform adoption for major Indian consumer brands.
paragraph2: Founded in 2025 by ex-Flipkart and Affle executives Sankalp Mehrotra, Anurag Singh, and Sharad Chitlangia, Kily develops autonomous AI agents to help consumer brands drive growth on ecommerce and quick commerce startups. The startup claims it has already partnered with leading brands including FMCG major ITC. Its agents integrate real-time signals from marketplaces with the client brand’s objectives, operating constraints, and context to automate workflows and decide. It can help brands optimise variables like product visibility, advertising efficiency, pricing and inventory availability.
paragraph3: “Brands and online sellers today operate in an increasingly fragmented ecosystem, where growth and profitability depend on making thousands of decisions across marketplaces every day. Kily is built to bring autonomy to commerce management, enabling brands and their partners to execute faster, make better decisions and scale profitably,” cofounder and CEO Mehrotra said. The investment comes at a time when businesses across industries are aggressively turning towards AI to streamline operations and manual workflows. And investors are increasingly taking note of platforms providing such solutions.
paragraph4: In the Indian context, there’s no better example than that of Emergent, whose AI agents allow entrepreneurs and small businesses to build software and websites without deep technical knowledge or experience. The startup became India’s third homegrown AI unicorn and sixth unicorn of 2026 when it raised $130 Mn in a Series C funding round earlier this year. Another prominent name in the emerging Indian AI space is Sarvam, which also joined the unicorn club this year after raising $234 Mn as part of its $300 Mn Series B funding round. Additionally, the startup hosted the first edition of its developer conference, Sarvam Epoch, this week, where it unveiled its ambitions of building an end-to-end AI stack.
paragraph5: Freehand, a startup focusing on agentic AI for enterprise supply chain operations, raised $75 Mn just last week as well. Zooming out, Indian AI startups raised $676 Mn across 57 deals in the first half of 2026, per Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report’. This capital inflow amounted to a 4X jump compared to the same period last year.

title: Pre-dawn emails and empty desks: inside the sudden layoffs at Visa India
title_bn: Pre-dawn emails and empty desks: inside the sudden layoffs at Visa India
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Visa layoffs show how AI is changing employment in multinational technology companies, with automation, tighter spending and workloads shifting months before thousands of roles were eliminated.
paragraph1: SummaryThe Visa layoffs show how AI is changing employment in multinational technology companies, with automation, tighter spending and workloads shifting months before thousands of roles were eliminated.On an ordinary day, a Visa Inc. employee would log in, pick up work from the previous day and go through emails and routine tasks. In recent months, some found themselves with more time on hand as automation took over parts of their jobs.Few, however, expected the first email of the day to be their last in the company: from human resources informing them that they had been laid off. For employees in India, the emails came between 4 am and 5 am on 29 July.Visa, the $40 billion San Francisco-based payments company, said on 28 July that it would cut about 7% of its workforce, roughly 2,600 roles. Chief executive officer (CEO) Ryan McInerney told employees the reductions were meant to drive efficiency.McInerney said on an earnings call on 28 July that AI is changing how work gets done at Visa.“Today, we announced that we are eliminating roles, with the majority being in our technology and product teams, to ensure that we are continuing to position Visa for future growth,” the CEO said. “Now, as we enter the era of agentic AI, we are going beyond AI assistance and harnessing the power of AI to execute work and tasks with our supervision.”He said agentic commerce will expand the company’s addressable market and drive growth for Visa.
paragraph2: Agentic commerce refers to the emerging use of autonomous AI agents to research, select, negotiate and make purchases on behalf of humans.Visa did not say how many of the roles being eliminated would be in India, its largest technology base outside the US. Its global headcount rose about 8% in fiscal 2025 to roughly 34,100. While the number of employees in India is not public, the company said in a statement in 2024 that its workforce exceeds 3,500 employees here.Whole teams hitVisa operates corporate, business and major technology hubs in India from Bengaluru and Mumbai, with additional corporate presence in Chennai and Hyderabad. Bengaluru is the company’s primary large-scale technology and software development centre.Mint spoke to six former and current employees from India to piece together what happened last week. All of them spoke on condition of anonymity, not wanting to jeopardize their job prospects.Visa did not respond to queries sent by Mint at publishing time.The cuts were deep enough to hollow out whole teams. On one India team of 28 people, 10 were let go, employees said. Seniority did not help.
paragraph3: Among those who lost their jobs were a director with about two decades at the company and a senior director with 21 years, along with several long-serving engineering managers.Severance packages varied widely and came with roughly 15 to 30 days of notice.“Some are getting a lot and some are getting less,” one employee said on condition of anonymity as they were not authorized to speak publicly.Although they were asked to serve notice periods, many employees had to hand over their ID cards and laptops and their access to company email was removed by Friday. The Bengaluru office emptied out within days. On Friday, people had been scuffling about to find places to sit. By Wednesday the place was dead silent.“Seeing your colleagues’ empty tables hurts a lot, and you can be the next any time,” said an employee who kept their job but lost their manager. The experience was draining, they said, even for those who were safe.Several of those laid off turned down invitations from former teammates for a farewell.“When I reached out to all of them, most of them were not ready to come,” one employee said. They did not want anything to do with the company that had just let them go.
paragraph4: Impact of AIThe Visa job cuts show how AI is slowing the pace of hiring and taking over or supplementing some roles in companies. Goldman Sachs, in a 28 July report, said 8% to 12% of India's non-agricultural employment is at risk of substitution from generative AI and 42% to 48% of jobs are more likely to be complemented by it, closer to augmentation than displacement.It found that job cuts in Indian technology have been concentrated in the six largest listed IT services firms, which shed a net 64,000 roles out of 1.7 million, while the rest of the sector, including global capability centres like Visa's in Bengaluru, added 700,000 people in three years.“For instance, in financial services, Gen-AI can complement analyst roles by automating some form of basic modelling, but may completely substitute routine back-office functions like basic compliance checks,” Goldman Sachs said in the report.The advent of AI has also led companies to reduce hiring. Total new hires at nine of the 30 Sensex companies fell 27% between from FY24 to FY26, Mint reported on Monday.The cuts at Visa did not come out of nowhere, employees said, even if the timing was a surprise. Over the preceding months, contractor hiring was pulled back and spending on outside software vendors was cut with the justification that AI could replace some of it.Token limitsIn July, caps appeared on AI tool usage where access had been open before. Developers in the US said they were expected to use large language models for their work, then handed a $1,500 monthly limit on the tokens they could consume.“This is the fourth such cost-cutting measure within the last quarter,” a Bengaluru-based employee said.
paragraph5: The contradiction is not lost on the people in Visa. AI is simultaneously the reason costs have escalated and the justification offered for the headcount reduction.“It's making us more efficient but we are not seeing the impact that is expected by the CXOs,” the employee said. “On the other hand, the cost has gone out of hand.”The scale of that spending is not in dispute.Visa consumed about 1.9 trillion AI tokens a month as of March, twice what it had used in February, Business Insider reported on 10 April. Four months later, in a follow-up report by Business Insider, employees were being metered.Visa's layoffs are not the first of its kind in the payments industry. In January, Mastercard said it would cut 4% of its global workforce, or about 1,400 employees. Chief financial officer Sachin Mehra said on an earnings call the layoffs would “free up capacity to further invest in our strategic priorities.” During the call, Mastercard CEO Michael Miebach introduced “agentic commerce” as a key growth pillar for 2026.

title: The studio behind Pokémon struggles to find its voice in Beast of Reincarnation
title_bn: The studio behind Pokémon struggles to find its voice in Beast of Reincarnation
author: TechPulse
excerpt: You have to imagine that the team at Game Freak is bursting with ideas. The studio puts out new mainline Pokémon adventures with a machinelike precision. But every so often it launches a curious experiment, whether it's an action title about a m
paragraph1: You have to imagine that the team at Game Freak is bursting with ideas. The studio puts out new mainline Pokémon adventures with a machinelike precision. But every so often it launches a curious experiment, whether it’s an action title about a militarized elephant or turning horse races into a card game, showing that it’s capable of more than the latest generation of pocket monsters. That’s part of what makes the idea of Beast of Reincarnation so enticing. Here is an established studio breaking free of the franchise it has become known for to make its take on a blockbuster action game. Unfortunately new ideas are in short supply in Beast, and aside from its slick action, there’s little that hasn’t been done before.Beast of Reincarnation takes place exactly 2,000 years in the future in a postapocalyptic vision of Japan that blends sci-fi and magic. Humans still exist, though many of them transferred their consciousness to robotic golems in order to survive the calamity that ruined the world. The real problem is that a mysterious blight has infected the landscape, turning wildlife into vicious, mutated monsters. Even worse: This seems to portend the return of the titular beast, a powerful creature that, as its name implies, appears to be immortal.
paragraph2: You play as a wandering mercenary-type named Emma who has the ability to absorb the powers of fallen mutants, and soon she’s tasked with traversing the world to power up so that she can take down the beast for good.It’s not a bad setup for an action game, as it gives you a reason to keep moving forward. Emma is constantly on the hunt for the next big creature that she can use to get stronger before taking on her final task. Beast of Reincarnation isn’t an open-world game, but instead is divided into a series of big locations that you travel between as the story progresses.Image: FictionsThe standout feature of the game is its action. Emma is a speedy samurai type, wielding a blade and various bows. At first, Beast seems like Dark Souls or Elden Ring, a game built around dodging and parrying, with little room for error. But as you unlock new powers, it proves to be something a little different. Emma’s signature ability is that vines and plants can grow out of her hair. This sounds weird, but it’s also incredibly useful; she can build bridges to traverse big gaps, or use her hair like a grappling hook to reach locations up high.
paragraph3: She also has an adorable and gigantic magical dog companion who follows her everywhere and provides a hand with combat and tedious chores like collecting loot.Emma’s powers are especially helpful in battle. Slowly she gains abilities that let her zip around the battlefield, using her hair to quickly gain ground on an enemy, deliver an attack from above, or team up with her powerful pup for a devastating blow. Her hair can even improve your stealth: At one point I unlocked a skill that caused tall plants to sprout wherever I crouched, temporarily giving me some cover before delivering a silent kill. It takes a few hours for things to open up, but eventually Beast’s combat has plenty of room for freedom and creativity.The same can’t be said for the rest of the experience. Initially, Beast’s postapocalyptic world is compelling because it’s full of mystery. You know almost nothing about the history of the world, but there are hints of interesting dynamics, like the human-infused machines and how they evolved differently from flesh-and-blood people. But Beast pushes the idea of mystery to a frustrating extreme. Everything in this game is mysterious: the landscape, Emma herself, her two human travel companions, her giant dog, the little girl that only Emma can see, the other wandering fighters she encounters in the world.
paragraph4: I love a story that is full of secrets and intrigue, but I barely understood what I was even doing in Beast until at least a dozen hours into the game. It doesn’t help that the game hides explanations of many of its key elements in a tutorial menu. And when you do finally get answers to the big mysteries, they’re mostly underwhelming.Image: FictionsThe story isn’t the only place that feels underdeveloped or uninspired. There are a number of gameplay elements — like the ability to grow your own food, and a weapon upgrade system — that are so simple that it’s easy to forget about them altogether. Meanwhile, the level design is incredibly straightforward, making exploration a bore, particularly when it comes to the dead-simple platforming sections. The game’s skill tree is even a literal tree.But the real issue with Beast of Reincarnation is that it is full of ideas that already exist elsewhere. The story is like a watered-down version of Nier: Automata’s heartrending postapocalypse, while the boss battles feel ripped out of Monster Hunter (with designs straight from its contemporary Wild Hearts and one specific creature that looks identical to a Stranger Things demodog). Your mobile home base functions much like the one in Death Stranding — you can even shower — and it looks just like an AT-ST from Star Wars.
paragraph5: Everywhere you go, there’s something from a different game or movie.This is especially disappointing because there is so much potential in Beast of Reincarnation. Not only is the combat thrilling, but, as derivative as it is, the game still manages to create an incredible sense of melancholic moodiness through its sound and visuals. But it never delivers on that; I was excited to learn about the strange religions and customs that were developed by isolated groups of golem, for instance, but the revelations were all surface level and quickly brushed aside.That sums up much of the Beast experience: There are flashes of excitement and intrigue, but mostly you’ve seen all of this before. At least there’s more Pokémon on the way.Beast of Reincarnation launches on August 4th on the PS5, Xbox, and PC.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.
